The conjunction "ところで" is placed at the beginning of a sentence to change the topic. Unlike "実は", "とこ
ろで" usually introduces a new topic completely unrelated to the previous one (examples ① and ②). In
some cases, what follows "ところで" can also be a related question about the preceding content (example
① A：今日も天気がいいですね。ところで、昨日の試合の結果はどうでし
た？／The weather is nice again today. By the way, how did yesterday's match turn out?
B：勝ちましたよ。／(We) won!
② A：スパイダーマンはかっこいいですよね。／Spider-Man is so cool, isn't he?
B：うん、かっこいい。ところで、スパイダーマンのスパイダーはどん
な意味ですか。／Yeah, he is. By the way, what does the "spider" in Spider-Man
mean?
③ ジョージ：３時なので、１時半ごろに出発しましょうか。／It starts at 3, so
shall we leave around 1:30?
由 加：わかりました。ところで、ジョージさんは今、時間がありま
すか。／Sure. By the way, George, do you have time now?
source_file: 初级上/27.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第16课.md

title: Plain forms of verbs
body_lines: Lesson 13 covered the plain forms of nouns and adjectives. Like noun sentences and adjective sentences, verb-final
verb sentences also have corresponding polite and plain forms.
Among them, "Vる (verb dictionary form)", and "Vない" and "Vなかっ
た" related to the verb imperfective form will be detailed in Grammar 2 and 3 of this lesson. Here the polite and plain forms of verbs are summarized in
Table 17.
Table 17-1: Four-quadrant comparison of polite and plain verb sentences
Affirmative  Negative
Present  Polite: V ます。  Polite: Vません。
Future  Plain: Vる (verb dictionary form)  Plain: Vない。
Polite: V ました。  Polite: Vませんでした。
Past
Plain: V た。  Plain: Vなかった。
Polite style is mostly used in formal settings; its tone is formal and courteous, so it is also called "polite style" — in Japanese,
"丁寧語". In spoken settings, plain style sounds more casual and intimate and is mostly used in conversations among friends or family;
in written settings, plain style emphasizes a more argumentative or declarative tone, so in writing it
is mostly used for papers, news reports, and the like.
source_file: 初级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第17课.md

title: V る (verb dictionary form)
body_lines: The affirmative plain form in the Japanese non-past tense is the verb's "dictionary form", also called the "verb original
form" or "verb basic form". This is the most basic form of the verb; since dictionary entries appear in this
form, it is usually called the "dictionary form". For example:
① 敬体：スマホでウェブサイトを閲覧します。／Browse websites on a phone.
Plain form: スマホでウェブサイトを閲覧する。／Browse websites on a phone.
② 敬体：よく徹夜します。／Often stay up all night.
Plain form: よく徹夜する。／Often stay up all night.
source_file: 初级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第17课.md

title: V ない (verb imperfective/nai-form)
body_lines: The negative plain form of a verb is formed by attaching the negative auxiliary ない to the verb.
Generally called the "nai-form" or "negative form" of the verb, also the "imperfective form".
The rules for attaching ない to verbs are as follows:
Group I (godan) verbs:
Change the final kana of the verb from the u-row to the a-row, then add ない. Note that
for type I verbs ending in う, change the final う to わ before adding ない.
For example:
使う：つかう→わ＋ない＝使わない
歩く：あるく→か＋ない＝歩かない
帰る：かえる→ら＋ない＝帰らない
Group II (ichidan) verbs:
Remove the final kana る, then add ない. For example:
見る：みる＋ない＝見ない
食べる：たべる＋ない＝食べない
集める：あつめる＋ない＝集めない
Group III (irregular) verbs:
① Suru-verb: する. Change する to し, then add ない. That is:
する：する→し＋ない＝しない
利用する：利用する→し＋ない＝利用しない
② Kuru-verb: 来る. Change 来る to 来, then add ない. That is:
来る：来る→こ＋ない＝来ない
Note that the negative form of ある is not あらない, but the adjective な
① この週末は家に帰らない。／(I'm) not going home this weekend.
② 今の学生はあまり運動しない。／Students these days don't exercise much.
The plain form of "V ませんでした" is the past tense of "V ない", i.e., "V なかった".
③ 宿題が多くて、昨夜、あまり寝なかった。／There was so much homework that I barely slept last night.
④ A：昨日のビールは？／What about yesterday's beer?
B：冷蔵庫だよ。／In the fridge.
A：ビールは冷蔵庫になかったよ。／The beer wasn't in the fridge.
source_file: 初级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第17课.md

title: Verb attributive form
body_lines: A verb can also modify a noun as an attributive modifier, called the "verb attributive form" — the form of a verb connecting to a
substantive (noun). The verb attributive form is exactly the same as the verb's plain form; choose the appropriate form according to the
tense and meaning. For example:
① 授業の予習や復習、課題をやる時間。／Time for class preparation and review, and for doing assignments.
② 明日行く場所はどこですか。／Where is the place (you're) going tomorrow?
③ 雨なので、飛行機が飛ばない可能性があります。／Because of the rain, the plane may
not fly.
source_file: 初级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第17课.md

title: N (period) に N (quantity) V <frequency>
body_lines: The particle に follows a noun expressing a period (usually a time span), indicating the frequency or quantity
of an action within that period. Equivalent to "per ..." in English.
① 週に3回運動する。／Exercise 3 times a week.
② ２か月に1回ぐらい映画を観る。／Watch a movie about once every two months.
③ 1年に1回中国へ帰る。／Go back to China once a year.
source_file: 初级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第17课.md

title: N についての N <about>
body_lines: In Lesson 15 we learned "Nについて", which follows a noun to introduce a topic, translatable as "about
...". "Nについて" can also be followed by の to qualify noun 2. Can be translated as "about
① こちらは大学生のライフスタイルについてのアンケートです。／This
is a survey about university students' lifestyles.
② このウェブサイトには、来 週 の口頭試験についての 情 報はない。／
This website has no information about next week's oral exam.
③ 来週は期末試験なので、明日から経済学についての本を読む。／Because
the final exam is next week, (I) will start reading a book about economics tomorrow.
source_file: 初级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第17课.md

title: ほとんど（/あまり）V ない
body_lines: As an adverb, ほとんど is mostly paired with the negative form of verbs. Can be translated as "hardly
(not) ...". Similar in usage is the adverb あまり, which can also be paired with the negative form of verbs
and can be translated as "(not very) ...".
① インターネットや SNS はほとんど利用しません。／Hardly use the internet
or social media.
② 漫画はときどき読みますが、アニメはほとんど見ません。／I read manga from time to
time, but I hardly watch anime.
③ Eメールはあまり使いません。／Don't use email much.
④ 梅雨の季節はあまり晴れません。／It rarely clears up during the rainy season.
source_file: 初级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第17课.md

title: N + particle + の + N
body_lines: Besides directly connecting two nouns (e.g., 私の車, 日本語の
本), the possessive particle の can also follow certain particles with concrete meanings (such as で, と, から, へ,
まで), combining with them to modify a noun. For example:
友達と食事する → 友達との食事
明日からゴールデンウィークが始まる → 明日からのゴールデンウィーク
デパートで買い物する → デパートでの買い物
大学の授業などに出席する → 大学の授業などへの出席
Note that there is no "N にの N" form. To express "toward ... (destination, direction) ...",
use the form "N への N".
① 雨の影響で、外国からの観光客が減少しました。／Due to the rain, foreign
tourists have decreased.
② 後輩との食事会はとても楽しかったです。／The dinner with my juniors was very
enjoyable.
③ 台風の影響で、香港へのフライトはキャンセルになりました。／
Due to the typhoon, the flight to Hong Kong was cancelled.
source_file: 初级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第17课.md

title: N や N など ＜enumeration; listing＞
body_lines: The particle や is used to list two or more things, and など means "etc.". The
two can be used together in the form "N や N など", translatable as "... and ... etc.". They can also
be used separately.
① インターネットやSNSなど／internet, social media, etc.
② A：デパートに何がありますか。／What is in the department store?
B：映画館や本屋などがあります。／There's a movie theater, a bookstore, and so on.
③ A：いつもどこで服を買いますか。／Where do you usually buy clothes?
B：ユニクロやタオバオで買います。／I buy them at Uniqlo, Taobao, etc.
source_file: 初级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第17课.md

title: お/ご + N <prefixes>
body_lines: "お" and "ご" are both prefixes. "お" is mostly attached before native Japanese words, showing respect for the listener or a third
party, or referring to things related to the listener, such as お名前 or お国. It can also
express the speaker's polite tone, as in お店 or お知らせ.
"ご" is mostly attached before Sino-Japanese nouns, or action-related Sino-Japanese words, showing respect for the listener or the person in the topic.
For example: ご両親, ご利用, ご協 力.
source_file: 初级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第17课.md

title: あげる/くれる/もらう <Giving/receiving verbs>
body_lines: Unlike Chinese, Japanese uses different words for "give" depending on the subject. The most
representative are "あげる", "くれる", and "もらう". This set of verbs expresses the giving and
receiving of things, and they are called "giving/receiving verbs". The specific rules are as follows:
Ⅰ. N (giver/I) は N (receiver) に N (thing) をあげる
"あげる" means "to give". It is used when "I" give something to someone else. When neither N is
"me", only two relationships are possible between the two Ns:
・Both Ns are at the same psychological distance from the speaker (as in example ②).
・The speaker feels psychologically closer to one N (as in example ③).
① （わたしは）彼女に花をあげました。／I gave my girlfriend flowers.
② 日本では、バレンタインデーには女性が男性にチョコレートをあげ
ます。／In Japan, girls give boys chocolate on Valentine's Day.
③ 妹 が友達にお土産をあげました。／My younger sister gave her friend a souvenir.
Besides "あげる", "やる" also means "to give", and its usage is basically
the same as "あげる". "やる" tends to emphasize giving to people of lower status than the speaker (such as one's
younger siblings) or to things (such as flowers, birds, pets). However, it is rarely used in modern Japanese.
④ 花に水をやります。／Water the flowers.
Ⅱ. N (giver) は N (receiver/me) に N をくれる
"くれる" also means "to give". But unlike "あげる", "くれる" refers to
someone else giving something to "me" (as in example ⑤). Therefore, the subject must always be "someone else". When
neither N is "me", only one relationship is possible: compared with one N, the speak-
er feels psychologically closer to the other N (as in example ⑥).
⑤ お 正 月に祖父がお年玉を（わたしに）くれました。／At New Year's, my grand-
father gave me New Year's gift money.
⑥ 社長が 妹 に花をくれました。／The company president gave my younger sister flowers.
Ⅲ. N (receiver/I) は N (giver) に/から N をもらう
"もらう" means "to receive". It expresses that "I" receive something from someone. For receiving
from someone, the "giver" is followed by the particle "に" or "から". When using "もらう",
the subject must be "I" (as in example ⑦). When neither N is "me", only one relation-
ship is possible: the speaker feels psychologically closer to one N than the other (as in the question in example ⑧).
⑦ （わたしは） 妹 にプレゼントのアドバイスをもらいました。／I; me
I got advice about the gift from my younger sister.
⑧ 佐藤：中村さんは李さんにどんなプレゼントをもらいましたか。
／What did Xiao Li give you?
中村：（わたしは）由加ちゃんからかわいいハンカチをもらいまし
た。／She gave me a very beautiful handkerchief.
"いただく" also means "to receive"; it is the humble form of "もらう". When
the speaker wants to express respect toward the giver, "もらう" can be replaced with "いただく",
which sounds more polite and formal.
⑨ みなさんから素敵なプレゼントをたくさんいただきました。／I received many
wonderful presents from everyone.
In Japanese, different giving/receiving verbs must be used according to person restrictions, and this
is one reason why Japanese often omits the subject. In fact, in Japanese, from the predicate verb alone, together with the
surrounding context, the listener can easily tell who the subject of the sentence refers to.
source_file: 初级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第18课.md

title: V ます形＋たい
body_lines: "たい" follows the masu-stem of a verb to express desire, equivalent to "(I) want to (do)...".
"たい" conjugates according to the rules for i-adjectives.
① あの会社で働きたいです。／I want to work at that company.
② 今日はあまり出かけたくないです。／I don't really want to go out today.
③ 遊びに行きたかったのですが、台風で止めました。／I wanted to go out and have fun, but
I decided not to because of the typhoon.
When the verb is transitive and takes an object marked with "を", that object can also be marked with "が"
instead.
④ おいしいものが食べたいです。／I want to eat something delicious.
The pattern "V masu-stem + たいです" is fairly strictly restricted by person and is generally used for the first person
(so the subject is often omitted). Also, asking about the second or third
person's wishes with the question form "V たいですか" is not very polite. Especially when the listener is of higher status or not very close to you,
you should try to avoid asking about their wishes with "V たいですか".
⑤ ○ 今日はあの人に会いたくありません。／I don't want to see that person today.
⑥ △ 何が食べたいですか。／What do you want to eat?
⇒ ○ お昼ご飯は何がいいんですか。／What would you like for lunch?
source_file: 初级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第18课.md

title: 〜か分かりません。
body_lines: Pattern: V (plain form) + か分かりません。
A (i-adjective, plain form) + か分かりません。
Ⅰ
A (na-adjective, plain form) + か分かりません。 (※A だ + か分かりません。)
Ⅱ Ⅱ
N (plain form) + か分かりません。 (※N だ + か分かりません。)
A plain-form question containing a question word followed by "分かりません" indicates something you don't know;
equivalent to "I don't know...". A plain-form question is generally formed with the plain form of a verb or i-adjective, or
a noun or na-adjective stem followed by the question particle "か".
① 新幹線の切符をどこで買うか分かりません。／I don't know where to buy Shinkan-
sen tickets.
② いつ雨が降るか分かりません。／I don't know when it will rain.
③ 中村さんの傘はどれか分かりません。／I don't know which one is Nakamura's umbrella.
source_file: 初级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第18课.md

title: ずつ
body_lines: The particle "ずつ" follows a quantity word or degree adverb, and expresses doing something repeatedly in fixed amounts,
or distributing equally in the same amount or proportion.
① 1人ずつ発言する。／Speak one by one.
② 日本語が少しずつ上手になりました。／My Japanese has improved little by little.
③ みかんを一人3個ずつあげます。／Give each person 3 mandarin oranges.
source_file: 初级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第18课.md

title: N にする <Choice>
body_lines: A noun followed by "にする" expresses choosing one thing from among many options. Equivalent to "choose..."
or "decide on...". Often used when ordering food, shopping, etc.
① A：お飲み物はどうなさいますか。／What would you like to drink?
B：ビールにします。／I'll have a beer.
② どの色がいいかわからなかったから、一色ずつにしました。／I didn't know which color was best, so I got one of each color.
③ A：今日のお昼は何にしましょうか。／What shall we have for lunch today?
B：私はラーメンが食べたいです。ラーメンにしましょうよ。／I want ramen. Let's have ramen.
source_file: 初级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第18课.md

title: Adjective continuative form
body_lines: Pattern: i-adjective A い→く + V
Ⅰ
na-adjective A + に + V
Ⅱ
The "adjective continuative form" is the form in which an adjective is followed by an inflecting word (i.e., a verb). With its continuative
form, an adjective can modify a verb, describing the manner in which the action proceeds or how it is carried out. In other words, this
is the adverbial use of adjectives. When an i-adjective is followed by a verb, its final "い" changes to "く"
before the verb; when a na-adjective is followed by a verb, "に" is added to its stem before the verb.
① 皆さんからの質問に親切に答えます。／I answer everyone's questions kind-
ly.
② お皿をきれいに洗いました。／I washed the dishes clean.
③ 早く走りましょう。／Let's run faster.
source_file: 初级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第18课.md

title: 〜ので、〜 <Cause/result II>
body_lines: Pattern: V (plain form) + ので、〜
A (i-adjective, plain form) + ので、〜
Ⅰ
A (na-adjective, plain form) + ので、〜 (※A だ → な + ので、〜)
Ⅱ Ⅱ
N (plain form) + ので、〜 (※N だ → な + ので、〜)
"ので" can be used mid-sentence to state a reason. In Lesson 12 we already learned the use of a noun fol-
lowed by "ので" to state a reason. This lesson further extends the word classes that can precede "ので"
to others: "ので" can also follow the plain form of a verb or i-adjective, or a na-adjective stem,
to state a reason arising from objective circumstances. Note, however, that for nouns and na-adjectives in the first quadrant (i.e., the non-past af-
firmative form), when their plain ending is followed by "ので", "だ" must be replaced with "な",
forming "N なので" or "A なので".
Ⅱ
① 頭が痛いので、早く帰りたいです。／I have a headache, so I want to go home early.
② 海外にいるので、参加ができません。／Because I'm overseas, I can't attend.
③ 発音があまりきれいじゃないので、たくさん練習したいです。／Because my
pronunciation isn't very good, I want to practice a lot.
④ ここは、今人気のお店なので、予約が難しいです。／This is a popular
restaurant right now, so it's hard to get a reservation.
source_file: 初级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第18课.md

title: とんでもないです。
body_lines: The original meaning of "とんでもない" is "completely unexpected, unreasonable". From this it extends to
negating the other person's statement; it can be translated as "not at all" or "don't mention it".
source_file: 初级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第18课.md

title: お誕 生 日、おめでとうございます。
body_lines: “おめでとうございます” means “congratulations.” “ございます” is used to express
politeness and can be left untranslated in Chinese. Between very close acquaintances, “ございます” may also be
omitted. Before “おめでとうございます”, you can also add the occasion being congratulated, such as “お
誕生日” (birthday), “ご結婚” (marriage), “ご入社” (joining a company), “ご就 職” (starting a job), etc.
source_file: 初级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第18课.md

title: よかった。
body_lines: Means “what a relief / thank goodness.” It is mostly an inner exclamation
of joy when something the speaker was worried about did not happen.
source_file: 初级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第18课.md

title: V て (verb second conjunctive form)
body_lines: Adding “て” to a verb forms the “verb te-form”; in Japanese school grammar it is also called the “verb second conjunctive form.”
The rules for changing a verb when followed by “て” are as follows:
Group I (godan) verbs:
The final kana of the verb changes according to the following four rules:
① For verbs ending in “う”, “つ”, or “る”, change “う”, “つ”, “る” to “っ”,
then add “て”. For example:
使う：つかう→っ＋て＝使って
待つ：まつ→っ＋て＝待って
送る：おくる→っ＋て＝送って
② For verbs ending in “く”, change “く” to “い”, then add “て”. For example:
書く：かく→い＋て＝書いて
泳ぐ*：およぐ→い＋で＝泳いで
*Verbs ending in “ぐ” are followed by “で”
③ For verbs ending in “す”, change “す” to “し”, then add “て”.
話す：はなす→し＋て＝話して
④ For verbs ending in “む”, “ぶ”, or “ぬ”, change “む”, “ぶ”, “ぬ” to “ん”,
then add “で”.
飲む：のむ→ん＋で＝飲んで
呼ぶ：よぶ→ん＋で＝呼んで
死ぬ：しぬ→ん＋で＝死んで
*The te-form of “行く” is irregular: “行って”
Group II (ichidan) verbs:
Drop the final kana “る” of the verb, then add “て”. For example:
起きる：おきる＋て＝起きて
食べる：たべる＋て＝食べて
Group III (irregular) verbs:
① Sa-hen (irregular) verb: “する”. Change “する” to “し”, then add “て”. That is:
する：する→し＋て＝して
勉強する：勉強する→し＋て＝勉強して
② Ka-hen (irregular) verb: “来る”. Change “来る” to “来”, then add “て”. That is:
来る：来る→き＋て＝来て
source_file: 初级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第19课.md

title: V ている ＜continuation of an action (V ている-I)＞
category: continuation of an action (V ている-I)
body_lines: “V ている” has many uses and is a common Japanese pattern. In this lesson, “V ている”
indicates that an action is in progress; it is often used with adverbs like “今” and “ちょうど”, equivalent to the Chinese
“正在……” (“to be doing ...”). “V ている” is the plain form expressing this meaning; its polite form is “ていま
① A: 今、何をしていますか。／What are you doing now?
B: ピアノを弾いています。／I'm playing the piano.
② A: すみません。この問題がわからないのですが。／Sorry, I don't understand this question.
B：実は、わたしもこの問題について、ちょうど考えているんですよ。一緒に
考えましょう。／Actually, I'm thinking about that problem too. Let's think about it together.
③ 今、運転しながら、音楽を聴いています。／Right now I'm listening to music while driving.
source_file: 初级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第19课.md

title: V た
body_lines: Adding “た” to a verb expresses completion, past, etc.; it is the plain form of “V ました”.
The change rules for “V た” are the same as for the verb te-form: just change “て” to “た”. Example:
example:
読む→読んで→読んだ
聞く→聞いて→聞いた
食べる→食べて→食べた
勉強する→勉強して→勉強した
① 漢字の読み方を間違えた。／I got the kanji reading wrong.
② 鈴木さんはスマホをどこかに落とした。／Suzuki dropped his smartphone somewhere.
③ あっちこっち探したが、見つからなかった。／I looked everywhere but couldn't find it.
source_file: 初级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第19课.md

title: V て、V て、V ます。 ＜verb continuation (chūdan)＞
body_lines: When a sentence contains two or more verbs in a sequential relationship,
they are usually connected with “V て”. When several verbs are linked in one sentence, it indicates that the actions occur in sequence;
this ordering need not be translated in Chinese.
① 3時に起きて、勉強しました。／I got up at 3 in the morning and studied.
② 私は東京に行って、東 京タワーとスカイツリーを見たいです。／I; me
(I) want to go to Tokyo, and see Tokyo Tower and the Skytree.
③ インターネットで資料を調べて、パワーポイントを作ります。／I'll look up materials online and make a PowerPoint.
④ 朝起きて、シャワーを浴びて、会社へ行きます。／I get up in the morning, take a shower, and go to work.
source_file: 初级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第19课.md

title: V てください。 ＜request＞
body_lines: The verb te-form followed by “ください” expresses a request for someone to do something, equivalent to “please ....”
Japanese has many polite expressions, and there are many patterns for making requests. “V てくだ
さい” is mostly used for polite instructions or requests. Therefore, “V てください” is generally not used toward superiors.
① 今日はお疲れさまでした。ゆっくり休んでください。／Thanks for your hard work today. Please get some good rest.
② 電話番号を教えてください。／Please tell me your phone number.
③ 明日の10時半に来てください。／Please come at 10:30 tomorrow.
④ これは中国のお土産です。どうぞ、食べてください。／This is a souvenir from China. Please try some.
source_file: 初级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第19课.md

title: 〜つもりだ。 ＜intention; plan＞
body_lines: Pattern: V る＋つもりだ.
V ない＋つもりだ。
The verb dictionary form or nai-form followed by “つもりだ” expresses the speaker's intention, translatable as
“I intend to ...” / “I plan to ....” “V るつもりだ” is fairly strictly limited to the first
person. Using a question with “つもりだ” can sound impolite to the listener, so unless the relationship is close,
it should be avoided (as in example ③).
① この夏休みはノーベル 賞 の受 賞 作品を読むつもりです。／I plan to read Nobel Prize-winning works this
summer vacation.
② 明日からお酒をやめるつもりです。／I plan to quit drinking starting tomorrow.
③ ジョージさん、レポートは何について書くつもりですか。／George, what do you
plan to write your report about?
Also, for “have no intention of doing ...” / “not plan to ...”, use the verb nai-form followed by “つも
りだ”, for example:
④ この冬休みは帰国しないつもりです。／I don't plan to go back to my home country this winter vacation.
source_file: 初级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第19课.md

title: 〜予定だ。 ＜plan＞
body_lines: Pattern: V る予定だ.
N の予定だ。
Compared with the “〜つもりだ” pattern, “V る予定だ” is used to state plans that are basically fixed;
it is relatively objective and does not include the speaker's subjective will. Therefore, there are no strict
person restrictions, the tone is softer, and it can be translated as “plan to (do something)” or “be scheduled to (do something).”
① 李さんはジョージさんと一緒に村上夏樹先生の講演会に参加する予定
です。／Xiao Li and George plan to attend Murakami Natsuki's lecture together.
② 今週の土曜日、歌舞俎を見に行く予定です。／This Saturday, I plan to go see
kabuki.
③ 今回のプロジェクトは２週間の予定です。／This project is scheduled to take two weeks.
④ 明日は朝6時の飛行機に乗る予定です。／I'm scheduled to take the 6 a.m. flight tomorrow.
source_file: 初级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第19课.md

title: 〜 中
body_lines: “ 中 ” mostly attaches to Chinese-origin (kango) words with an action meaning to show the action is in progress; it is read “ち
ゅう”. For example, “営業 中 ” (open for business), “準備中” (preparing), “会議中” (in a meeting), etc.
① A: 近くのレストランは、今、やっていますか。／Is the restaurant nearby open
now?
B: はい、今営業 中 ですよ。／Yes, it's open right now.
② 会議中に、お邪魔してすみません。／Sorry to interrupt during the meeting.
③ 隣が工事中で、とてもうるさいです。／There's construction next door and it's very noisy.
source_file: 初级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第19课.md

title: こっち
body_lines: “こっち” is the colloquial form of “こちら”, meaning “my side / this way”, “this one”, etc. Like-
wise, there are also “そっち”, “あっち”, and “どっち”.
source_file: 初级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第19课.md

title: もしもし
body_lines: A set phrase when making a phone call, equivalent to “hello?” Besides “もしもし”, when answering the phone you can
also say “はい” followed by identifying yourself — your surname, or the name of your workplace or department,
etc.
source_file: 初级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第19课.md

title: お久しぶりです。
body_lines: Means “long time no see.”
source_file: 初级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第19课.md

title: 博物館の見学、楽しんでくださいね。
body_lines: Means “Enjoy your museum visit!” “〜を楽しんでください” means “please enjoy
...” / “have fun.”
source_file: 初级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第19课.md

title: では、またね。
body_lines: This is an expression used between close acquaintances when saying goodbye; the tone is informal and relaxed. It means “see
you.”
You can also add the date of the next meeting after “また”, e.g. “では、また明日ね” (“well, see you tomorrow”).
Young people in Japan today also shorten “では、またね” to “じゃね”, but this expression
should only be used between friends; it is inappropriate toward superiors or people you are meeting for the first time in formal settings.
source_file: 初级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第19课.md

title: Japanese verb aspect and its polite and plain forms
body_lines: “V ている” belongs to the category of “aspect (アスペクト)” in Japanese grammar and expresses
the state of an action (such as its continuation or completion). Besides the negative of “V ている”, “V ていない”,
“V ている” can also combine with the past tense to form “V ていた” or “V てい
なかった”. Table 20 summarizes the polite and plain forms related to “V ている”.
Table 20: Four-quadrant comparison of polite and plain forms of “V ている”
Affirmative  Negative
Present/future — Polite: Vています。 Polite: Vていません。
Plain: Vている。 Plain: Vていない。
Polite: Vていました。 Polite: Vていませんでした。
Past
Plain: Vていた。 Plain: Vていなかった。
① 朝からずっと曇っている。／It's been cloudy since morning.
② 地震の時、私は庭の掃除をしていた。／When the earthquake struck, I was cleaning the yard.
③ この夏休みは、ずっとマラソンの練習をしていた。／All through this summer vacation I was
training for the marathon.
④ 小さい時は、まだ日本語を習っていなかった。／When I was little, I
hadn't started learning Japanese yet.
source_file: 初级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第20课.md

title: V ている ＜continuation of a result (V ている-II)＞
category: continuation of a result (V ている-II)
body_lines: In Lesson 19 we learned the first use of “V ている”, expressing the continuation of an action.
This lesson continues with other uses of “V ている”. The second use: attached to instantaneous
verbs, it describes the continuation of the result after the action has occurred.
① 外は暗くなっています。／It's gotten dark outside.
② ガラスの窓が割れています。／The glass window is broken.
③ 兄は結婚しています。／My older brother is married.
source_file: 初级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第20课.md

title: V ている ＜habitual behavior (V ている-III)＞
body_lines: The third use of “V ている”: it expresses an action repeated over a recent period, habitual
behavior, or an action continued over a long period.
① 弟 は、大学のサークルでジャーナリストをやっています。／My younger brother works as a journalist
in his university club.
② 兄は今、アメリカに住んでいます。／My older brother is living in America now.
③ 今、パリでフランス料理を習っています。／I'm currently learning French cooking in Paris.
④ 彼と毎週会っています。／I meet him every week.
source_file: 初级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第20课.md

title: （まだ）V ていない
body_lines: The negative form of the durative “V ている” is “V ていない”; its polite form is “V ていま
せん”. It is often used with the adverb “まだ” and can be translated as “not (yet) ...”.
This pattern is mostly used as a negative answer to “もうV ましたか。” (“Have you already ...?”).
① A: 講演会はもう始まりましたか。／Has the lecture already started?
B: まだ始まっていませんよ。急いでください。／It hasn't started yet. Hurry up.
② A: 部長に電話しましたか。／Did you call the department manager?
B: いいえ、まだしていません。／No, not yet.
③ 論文のテーマをまだ決めていません。／I haven't decided on my thesis topic yet.
source_file: 初级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第20课.md

title: V る前（に） ＜before ...＞
body_lines: “前（に）” attaches to the verb dictionary form (example ①) or after a noun with an action meaning plus “の”
(example ②), and expresses doing some action before the preceding action occurs. It can be translated as “before
..., ...”. The “に” after “前” marks the time point of the following action and can sometimes be omitted.
① 食事をする前に、手を洗いましょう。／Let's wash our hands before eating.
② 食 事の前に、 食 器をテーブルに並べる。／Before the meal, set the tableware on the table.
③ この質問に答える前に、ちゃんと考えてください。／Before answering this question, please think carefully.
source_file: 初级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第20课.md

title: V てから ＜after ...＞
body_lines: The verb te-form followed by “から” expresses the sequence of actions and can be translated as “after (doing) ...,
(then do) ....”
① 口コミ情報をチェックしてから、商品を買います。／I check the online reviews first, and then
buy the product.
② 日本でお風呂に入るときは、体を洗ってから、入ります。／In Japan, when taking a bath,
you wash your body first and then get into the tub.
③ 上司に報告してから、レポートを書きます。／After reporting to my boss, I write the report.
source_file: 初级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第20课.md

title: (third person) V たがる/N をほしがる
body_lines: In previous lessons we learned “V たい” for wanting to do something (Lesson 18) and “N がほしいです” for wanting
something (Lesson 11), as well as the person restrictions on these two patterns. This lesson covers how
these two patterns are used with the third person.
When expressing a third person's desire to perform an action, the “V たがる” form is generally used.
“-たがる” is a derived verb from “-たい”. Note that with “V たがる”, the verb's object
is marked with “を” and cannot be changed to “が”.
① 兄はあのレストランのシェフになりたがっています。／My older brother wants to become the chef of that restaurant.
② 弟 は新しいカメラを買いたがっています。／My younger brother wants to buy a new camera.
“V たがる” expresses the subject's (third person) desire to perform an action; in contrast,
“N をほしがる” expresses the subject's (third person) desire to obtain something.
③ 弟 は新しいカメラをほしがっています。／My younger brother wants a new camera.
④ ジョージさんは村上夏樹先生のサインをほしがっている。／George wants Murakami Natsuki's autograph.
source_file: 初级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第20课.md

title: N が見える
body_lines: “見える” means “can see ....” This is an intransitive verb that inherently carries a potential meaning;
the object of such intransitive verbs is marked with “が”. Another verb with the same usage as “見える” is
“聞こえる”, translatable as “can hear ....”
① あそこの赤い看板が見えますか。／Can you see that red signboard over there?
② 今夜は星がよく見える。／The stars are clearly visible tonight.
③ 外はうるさくて、先生の話がよく聞こえません。／It's noisy outside, so I can't hear
what the teacher is saying very well.
④ 後ろの方は聞こえますか。／Can the people at the back hear?
source_file: 初级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第20课.md

title: わざわざ
body_lines: The adverb “わざわざ” means “to go out of one's way (to do something).” In this lesson, “わざわざ” carries
the nuance of “bothering to do (something unnecessary).”
① どうしてわざわざカメラを買うのですか。／Why go out of your way to buy a camera?
② わざわざ 車 で 5時間もかけて限定 商 品を買いに来た。／(They) drove 5 hours
out of their way just to buy the limited-edition item.
“わざわざ” is also used to comment on others' actions with the positive nuance of “taking the trouble to”, and is often paired with honorific
expressions. In this usage, it cannot be used by the speaker about their own actions. For example:
③ わざわざありがとうございました。／Thank you for going to all that trouble.
④ わざわざすみません。／Sorry to have made you go to all that trouble.
source_file: 初级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第20课.md

title: V ないでください。 ＜negative request (prohibition)＞
body_lines: “V ないでください” is the negative form of the request pattern “V てください”, and is mostly
used to express prohibition. It can be translated as “please don't ...”, “do not ...”, etc.
① ここではタバコを吸わないでください。／Please do not smoke here.
② 危ないですから、椅子に登らないでください。／It's dangerous, so please don't climb on the
chair.
③ 写真を撮らないでください。／Please do not take photos.
source_file: 初级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第21课.md

title: V てもいい ＜permission＞
body_lines: A verb followed by “てもいい” expresses permission for (the other party) to do something, equivalent to “you may
....” When “V てもいい” is used as a question, the subject is usually the first person (“わたし”) — the speaker
themselves — and is often omitted, equivalent to “may I ...?” Also, the “いい” in the pattern “V
てもいい” can sometimes be replaced with “大丈夫”.
① A：この本を借りてもいいですか。／May I borrow this book?
B：ええ、どうぞ。／Sure, go ahead.
② 来 週 のパーティーに彼女を連れてきてもいいですよ。／You may bring your girlfriend to next week's
party.
③ A：こちらの資 料 を印刷しても大 丈 夫ですか。／May I print this mate-
rial?
B：はい、大丈夫ですよ。／Yes, that's fine.
source_file: 初级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第21课.md

title: V なくてもいい ＜not necessary＞
body_lines: The verb nai-form followed by “なくてもいい” expresses permitting someone not to do something, translatable as “you don't
have to ...”, “it's all right not to ....”
① 返さなくてもいいです。／You don't have to return it.
② 重い本は明日、持ってこなくてもいいですよ。／You don't have to bring the heavy books
tomorrow.
③ 急ぎませんので、今日は決めなくてもいいですよ。／There's no rush, so you don't have to decide
today.
source_file: 初级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第21课.md

title: V てはいけない ＜prohibition＞
body_lines: A verb followed by “てはいけない” expresses prohibition, translatable as “must not ...”, “you are not allowed to
...”. It is mostly used for requirements from superiors to subordinates, or to state rules and discipline.
① 子供は夜遅くまで、外で遊んではいけないよ。／Children must not play outside until late at night.
② 図書館では飲み物を机の上に置いてはいけません。／In the library, you must not
leave drinks on the desk.
③ 食べ物を図書館に持ち込んではいけません。／Food must not be brought into the library.
source_file: 初级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第21课.md

title: V なければならない ＜have to; obligation＞
body_lines: The verb nai-form followed by “なければならない” means “must”, “have to”. It expresses
the necessity or obligation to do an action. Patterns with similar meanings to “V なければならない” include:
“V なくてはいけない”, “V なければいけない”, and “V なくてはな
らない”. In spoken language, “V なければ” can be shortened to “V なきゃ”, and “V なくては” can be short-
ened to “V なくちゃ”.
① 日本人の家に入る時、靴を脱がなければなりません。／When entering a Japanese
person's home, you must take off your shoes.
② 日本では後ろの座席もシートベルトを締めなければいけません。／In Japan, seatbelts must be fastened even in the back seat.
③ せっかくの休みですが、仕事が終わらないので、残業しなければなら
ないんです。／It's a rare day off, but because the work isn't finished,
I have to work overtime.
source_file: 初级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第21课.md

title: V ることができる ＜able to＞
body_lines: The verb dictionary form followed by “ことができる” expresses “being able to (do something).” Here,
“able” can mean either the ability to do something or having the conditions to do it, translatable as
“can ...”, “be able to ....” For example:
① ドイツ語を話すことができますか。／Can you speak German?
② レポートを書いたので、明日みんなに報告することができます。／Since I've finished writing the report, I can present it to everyone tomorrow.
Now that the report is written, I can report to everyone tomorrow.
③ おかげさまで、無事に退院することができました。／Thanks to you, I was able to
leave the hospital safely.
source_file: 初级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第21课.md

title: N だけ + particle ＜limitation＞
body_lines: “だけ” can attach to a noun to express limitation, translatable as “only”, “just”, etc. Depending on the
needs of the sentence, “だけ” can be followed by particles like “で”, “に”, “は”, “を”, “が”; when followed by “を” or
“が”, those particles can be omitted.
① 日本人の子供たちは平仮名だけで作文を書きます。／Japanese children write compositions using only hiragana.
② これだけはやめてください。／Just this one thing — please don't do it.
③ お金がないので、今日のお昼ご飯はサンドイッチだけで済ませます。
／Since I have no money, I'll make do with just a sandwich for lunch today.
source_file: 初级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第21课.md

title: けっこうです。
body_lines: In this lesson, “けっこうです” means “that's fine”, expressing approval by someone with the authority
to decide of another person's words or actions. Note that when expressing approval, “けっこうです”
cannot be used toward someone of higher status.
“けっこうです” can also be used to decline someone, translatable as “no thank you; I've had enough.”
When expressing refusal, “けっこうです” is a fairly polite expression and can also be used toward someone of higher sta-
tus. Which meaning “けっこうです” has must be judged from the context and the speaker's
tone. For example:
① A：紅茶をもう少しいかがですか。／Would you like some more tea?
B：もうけっこうです。／No, thank you (I've had enough).
② A：明日は来なくてもいいですか。／Is it all right if I don't come tomorrow?
B：はい、けっこうです。／I'm fine, thanks.
③ せっかくのお誘いですが、わたしはけっこうです。／I appreciate the kind
invitation, but I'll pass this time.
source_file: 初级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第21课.md

title: V る/V た時（に）
body_lines: Both the "verb ta-form" and the "verb dictionary form" can be followed by 時（に） to mean "at the time of
...". But note that the time points expressed by the "verb dictionary form" and the "verb ta-form" differ.
"V る時（に）" refers to something that happens while the preceding action is not yet complete (example ①), while "V た時
（に）" refers to something that happens at the point after the preceding action is complete (examples ②③).
① 友達の家に遊びに行く時に、お土産を買いました。／When (I) was about to go to a friend's house
to hang out, (I) bought a souvenir.
② 友達の家に遊びに行った時、みんなで餃子を作りました。／When we went to a friend's place to hang out, everyone made dumplings together.
③ 駅を出た時、人気のケーキを買いました。／When (I) came out of the station, (I) bought
the popular cake.
source_file: 初级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第22课.md

title: V たことがある <experience>
body_lines: "Verb ta-form" followed by ことがある expresses having had a certain experience, translatable as "have (once)
...". The negative form of this pattern is "V たことがない" (example ②). Also, when answering "〜
たことがありますか", you can use ある or ない.
① あの人は、確か前に会ったことがあります。／That person — I think I've met
(them) before.
② 日本で歌舞伎を見たことがありません。／I have never seen kabuki in Japan.
③ A：体育の授業で怪我をしたことがありますか。／Have you ever been injured in PE class?
B：はい、あります。／Yes, I have.
④ A：着物を着たことがありますか。／Have you ever worn a kimono?
B：いいえ、ありません。／No, I haven't.
The "V たことがある" pattern is mostly used for experiences long past or once had; it is not used to nar-
rate recent experiences (example ⑤).
⑤ ×私は、昨日、お寿司を食べたことがあります。
○私は、昨日、初めてお寿司を食べました。／I ate sushi for the first time yesterday.
source_file: 初级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第22课.md

title: V る/V ないことがある <sometimes; occasionally>
body_lines: In contrast to "V たことがある", the "verb dictionary form" or "verb nai-form" followed by "こと
がある" expresses that the action or situation sometimes occurs, translatable as "sometimes do/don't ...", "(occasionally)
there are times when ... / times when not ...".
① いつも寝る前にシャワーを浴びますが、朝起きてからシャワーを浴び
ることもあります。／I usually shower before bed, but sometimes
I shower after getting up in the morning.
② 梅雨の季節では、一週 間も晴れないことがある。／During the rainy season, sometimes
there isn't a single sunny day for a whole week.
③ 兄とは仲がいいのですが、喧嘩することもありますよ。／I get along well with my brother, but we
sometimes fight too.
④ ここの地域は、半年以上も雨が降らないことがある。／In this region, there are times when it
doesn't rain for more than half a year.
source_file: 初级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第22课.md

title: V ます形＋方
body_lines: "Verb masu-stem" followed by 方 forms a derived noun meaning "way of (doing) ...".
For example, 使い方 (way of using), 読み方 (way of reading), etc.
① 学び方についての本を探しています。／I'm looking for a book about ways of learning.
② このアプリの使い方がよくわかりません。／I don't really understand how to use this app.
③ 丁寧な話し方がとても大事です。／A polite way of speaking is very important.
source_file: 初级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第22课.md

title: N がする
body_lines: A noun followed by がする expresses a bodily sensation, such as a smell, sound, or taste. Often seen in 音が
する (a sound is made), 匂いがする (there is a smell), 味がする (there is a
taste), etc.
① 横のケーキ屋さんからとてもいい匂いがした。／From the cake shop next door came
a really nice smell.
② レモンは酸っぱい味がします。／Lemons taste sour.
③ スタバからいつもコーヒーのいい香りがします。／There's always a nice coffee aroma from
Starbucks.
source_file: 初级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第22课.md

title: N (place) を <starting point; passing through>
body_lines: The particle を follows a place noun and pairs with intransitive verbs of movement, passing, or departure (such as 電車を
降りる, 橋を渡る) to mark the starting point of movement or the
route passed through.
① あの人気のケーキ屋さんは駅を出てすぐです。／That popular cake shop is right
outside the station exit.
② 交差点を右に曲がってください。コンビニは左手にあります。／Turn right at the intersection. The convenience store is on the left.
③ 香港を経由してオーストラリアに行く。／Go to Australia via Hong Kong.
source_file: 初级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第22课.md

title: 〜でしょう <conjecture>
body_lines: Pattern: V plain form + でしょう
A (i-adjective) plain + でしょう
Ⅰ
A (na-adjective) plain (※ without 〜だ) + でしょう
Ⅱ
N plain (※ without 〜だ) + でしょう
A plain-style sentence (but for type II adjectives and nouns, drop the だ) followed by でしょう ex-
presses the speaker's conjecture, translatable as "... probably", "I suppose". The intonation of でしょう usually falls; it is often paired with adverbs like た
ぶん (probably) or きっと (surely). Its plain form is だろう.
① 初めは難しいでしょうね。／It must be hard at first.
② 明日は雨でしょう。／It will probably rain tomorrow.
③ ご両親もあなたの結婚を反対するでしょう。／Your parents will probably oppose your mar-
riage too.
④ 今頃はもうホテルに着いているだろう。／By now they should have arrived at the hotel.
source_file: 初级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第22课.md

title: 〜間、〜 <during ...>
body_lines: Pattern: N の間、〜
V ている間、〜
"〜間" expresses two states or actions continuing in parallel — that is, throughout the whole period
described in the first clause, the action in the second clause continues. The first clause can be a noun + の or "verb ている"
followed by 間, and the second clause usually ends with "V ていた". Can be translated as "during ..., (all along) ...".
① 夏休みの間、ずっとアメリカを旅行していました。／During the whole summer vacation (I) was
traveling in America.
② 母がご飯を作っている 間 、 私 はずっと横で手伝っていました。／While my mother was cooking, I kept
helping beside her.
③ バスを待っている間、ずっとスマホを見ていました。／While waiting for the bus, (I) kept
looking at my phone.
(cid:0)(cid:0)(cid:0)(cid:0)
source_file: 初级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第22课.md

title: かな <modal particle>
body_lines: The modal particle かな combines the question particle か with the exclamatory particle な.
Attached after a plain sentence or a noun, it expresses a question with a light exclamatory nuance, or an uncertain
tone when talking to oneself.
① かなりきつい仕事なので、あの人は一人でできるかな。／This is pretty demanding work — I wonder if he
can do it alone.
② もうそろそろ向こうに着くころかな。／I guess we'll be arriving (there) pretty soon.
③ 締め切りは確か来月の4日かな。／The deadline was the 4th of next month, if I remember right.
source_file: 初级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第22课.md

title: さあ、〜
body_lines: "さあ" is an interjection used to get the listener's attention and urge them to do something. For example:
① さあ、出発しましょう。／All right, let's go!
② さあ、見てください。／Come on, take a look!
source_file: 初级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第22课.md

title: 上がってください。
body_lines: When visiting a Japanese home, you usually take off your shoes at the entrance and step up one level before entering. There-
fore, the verb used for entering a room is 上がる. Besides 上がってください, an even more polite way to say "please come in"
is お上がりください. Of course, for places where you don't need to remove your shoes, such as offices
or shops, you can also use 入ってください or お入りください.
source_file: 初级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第22课.md

title: お邪魔します。
body_lines: This is a polite phrase meaning "excuse me for intruding". It is used when entering someone's private space, such as the host's
room or office.
① A：お邪魔します。／Excuse me (I'm coming in).
B：はい、どうぞ。／Yes, please come in.
source_file: 初级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第22课.md

title: 当たり
body_lines: "当たり" is the noun form of 当たる, meaning a hit or a success. In this lesson, George
says 当たり, meaning Yuka guessed right. Also, 当たり can describe a product or plan being a
hit or very popular. Young Japanese also use it to say they feel good about someone or something after experiencing it.
For example:
① 今年の担当は当たりだ。／This year's person in charge is a great pick.
② A：この店、口コミを見て選んだんですが、けっこう当たりでしたよ。
／I picked this place from reviews, and it turned out pretty good.
B：あ、ここ、知っています。最近人気なんですよね。／Ah, this place —
I know it. It's been popular lately.
source_file: 初级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第22课.md

title: 〜ても
body_lines: Pattern: V て + も
Aい→く＋ても
Ⅰ
A ＋でも
Ⅱ
N＋でも
The verb te-form followed by も, type I adjectives with the final い changed to く followed by ても,
and type II adjectives and nouns followed by でも, all form a concessive compound sentence, translatable as "even
① ジョージさんと中村さんは、並んでも食べたいケーキを持ってき
てくれました。／George and Nakamura brought me the cake worth queuing
for.
② 明日雨が降っても、遠足に行きます。／Even if it rains tomorrow, (we're) going on the excursion.
③ もうすぐ大事な試験ですから、眠くても勉強しなければなりませ
ん。／The important exam is coming soon, so even if I'm sleepy, I have to study.
④ 嫌いでも、野菜はちゃんと食べましょう。／Even if you don't like them, eat your vegetables
properly.
⑤ お金がないので、 週 末でも 働 きます。／Because I have no money, I work even on
weekends.
source_file: 初级下/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第23课.md

title: N (time point) までに <deadline>
body_lines: The particle までに follows a noun expressing a time point or a verb dictionary form, indicating that an action is completed before that time. Can be translated as "by ...".
① 会議は遅くても4時までに終わるだろう。／The meeting will end by 4 at the
latest.
② 大学を卒業するまでに、就 職先を決めたい。／Before graduating from university,
(I) want to decide on a job.
③ ３５歳までに結婚したいと思う。／I want to get married by 35.
source_file: 初级下/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第23课.md

title: 〜と言う ＜quotation＞
body_lines: The particle と marks quoted content and can be followed by verbs of saying, hearing, etc., such as 言う
(to say), 聞く (to hear), 聞く (to ask), 答える (to answer). Japanese also has direct and indirect
quotation. For example, the following dialogue:
由加：環 境 と経済の関連性についてはいかがですか。
鈴木：それはいいですね。
To objectively describe the two people's conversation using direct quotation, use the forms in examples ①–④. In writ-
ing, the quoted original sentence in a direct quotation is usually marked with 「」, and the sentence's style does not need to be
changed.
① 李さんは鈴木さんに「環境と経済の関連性についてはいかがです
か」と聞きました。／Li asked Suzuki: "How about writing about the relationship between the environment and
the economy?"
② 鈴木さんは「それはいいですね」と答えました。／Suzuki answered: "That's
great."
③ 李さんは「 新しい会社の人はみんな親切です」と言いました。／
Li said: "The people at the new company are all kind."
④ 日本では、食事をする前に「いただきます」と言います。／In Japan, people say "itadakimasu" before eating.
You can also express it with indirect quotation, as in examples ⑤–⑧. Indirect quotations generally don't need
marks to set off the quoted part, but the quoted part must be rewritten in plain style.
⑤ 李さんは鈴木さんに環 境 と経済の関連性についてはいかがかと
聞きました。／Li asked Suzuki how it would be to write about the relationship between the environment
and the economy.
⑥ 鈴木さんはそれはいいねと答えました。／Suzuki answered that it was great.
⑦ 李さんは新しい会社の人はみんな親切だと言いました。／Li said
that the people at the new company were all kind.
⑧ 佐藤さんは明日野球の試合があると言いました。／Sato said he has
a baseball game tomorrow.
source_file: 初级下/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第23课.md

title: 〜と思う
body_lines: The particle と marks the content of "thinking". "〜と思う" is mostly used in the first person to ex-
press the speaker's thoughts or opinions. "〜と思う" generally does not use direct-quotation form, so the content before と
must be in plain form. "〜と思う" can be translated as "(I) think ...",
"(I) believe ...", "(I) feel ...", etc.
① それはいいと思います。／I think that's good.
② ジョージさんは木曜日にもアルバイトがあると思います。／I think
George also has a part-time job on Thursday.
③ わたしはまだ結婚したくないと思います。／I don't want to get married yet.
④ そのやり方は効率的ではないと思います。／I don't think that way of doing it
is very efficient.
source_file: 初级下/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第23课.md

title: 〜かもしれない
body_lines: Pattern: plain sentence + かもしれない
※N だ+かもしれない
※A +だ+かもしれない
Ⅱ
"〜かもしれない" can be translated as "maybe ...". "〜かもしれない" follows a plain-style
sentence. But note in particular that nouns and type II adjectives first drop だ before adding かもし
れない". Compared with "〜でしょう/だろう", the possibility expressed by "〜かもしれない"
is lower, and it can even imply that the possibility may not exist at all.
① 寒い日がずっと続いていて、ちょっと風邪かもしれないです。／
The severe cold keeps going, so maybe I've caught a bit of a cold.
② ９時半の新幹線に間に合うかもしれないから、急ぎましょう。／
We might make the 9:30 Shinkansen — let's hurry.
③ 有名な会社に勤めているけど、 給 料 はほかの会社より少ないか
もしれない。／Although (he) works at a famous company, the salary might
be lower than at other companies.
source_file: 初级下/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第23课.md

title: 〜後（で）、〜
body_lines: Pattern: V た + 後（で）、〜
N の後（で）、〜
"Verb ta-form" or an action noun + の followed by 後（で） expresses doing one action
after another action, translatable as "after ..., ...".
① 少し練習した後で、みんなの前で発表します。／After a bit of practice,
(I'll) present in front of everyone.
② 授業の後で、電話します。／(I'll) call after class.
③ 食事の後で、カラオケに行きましょうか。／After the meal, shall we go to
karaoke?
④ アニメを見た後で、お風呂に入ります。／After watching anime, (I'll) take a bath.
source_file: 初级下/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第23课.md

title: N しか V ない ＜limitation＞
body_lines: The particle しか follows a noun and pairs with the negative form of a verb to form the meaning "only; just".
Although the predicate verb is negative, the sentence meaning is affirmative, limiting what comes before しか.
① お金持ちのお嬢さんは高級品しか使いません。／The rich family's daughter
only uses luxury goods.
② 晩ご飯は野菜サラダしか食べません。／For dinner (I) only eat vegetable salad.
③ この会社は社員が 2 人しかいません。／This company has only two
employees.
source_file: 初级下/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第23课.md

title: N だけでなく N も
body_lines: The particle だけ follows a noun to express limitation, meaning "only; just". A noun followed by "N だ
けでなく N も" can be translated as "not only N ... but N (also) ...".
① 漢字は中国人だけでなく、日本人も使います。／Kanji is used not only by the Chinese,
but by the Japanese too.
② ジブリのアニメーション映画はストーリーだけでなく、音楽も最高です。／Ghibli's animated films are great not only in story — the music
is also amazing.
③ ワンピースは日本だけでなく、海外でも人気が高いです。／“One Piece” is popular not only in Japan but overseas as well.
source_file: 初级下/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第23课.md

title: V てあげる/くれる/もらう
body_lines: In Lesson 18 we learned the verbs あげる/くれる/もらう for expressing the giving and receiving of things.
This lesson covers the use of these giving/receiving verbs after て as auxiliary verbs. Verbs
followed by てあげる/くれる/もらう express the giving and receiving of actions. The specific rules are as follows:
<Giving/receiving verb sentence I>
N (I / giver) は N (receiver) に V てあげる
<Giving/receiving verb sentence I> expresses doing something for someone else. When neither N nor N is "I",
only two relationships are possible between N and N:
・N and N are at the same psychological distance from the speaker.
・The speaker is psychologically closer to N.
Note, however, that the "V てあげる" pattern over-emphasizes that you deliberately did something for the other person,
which can make the listener feel they are being done a favor. So if the other person is not someone close to you,
avoid it as much as possible to prevent sounding rude (example ③). In such cases use "V ましょうか"
(example ④), which is more polite.
① 観光客に道を教えてあげます。／(I'll) give directions to the tourists.
② 由加さんはクラスメートに美味しい 中 華 料 理を作ってあげまし
た。／Yuka made delicious Chinese food for her classmates.
③ （×）先生、重いので、持ってあげます！
④ （○）先生、重いので、持ちましょうか。／Teacher, it's heavy — shall I
carry it for you?
<Giving/receiving verb sentence II>
N (giver) は N (I / receiver) に V てくれる
<Giving/receiving verb sentence II> expresses that someone else does something for you or for someone on your side,
i.e., "(someone) does ... (for me)". Here the giver of the action is the subject, and the receiver (usually "I")
is marked with に, but 私に is often omitted.
⑤ 日本人の友達が作文を直してくれました。／My Japanese friend corrected my ess-
ay.
⑥ 母は1人で私を育ててくれました。／My mother raised me all by herself.
<Giving/receiving verb sentence III>
N (I / receiver) は N (giver) に/から V てもらう
<Giving/receiving verb sentence III> expresses receiving someone's doing something for you. The subject of this pattern
is the receiver of the action, i.e., "I", and 私は is often omitted. The giver of the action is usually marked with に
or から. Both "V てくれる" and "V てもらう" can express that the speaker receives someone's doing some-
thing for them, i.e., the speaker is the beneficiary. But compared with "V てくれる", "V てもらう" more often
carries the nuance of being fortunate to "receive" someone's doing something for you. It therefore better highlights the speaker's gratitude
toward the giver of the action.
⑦ もう電車もバスもないので、友達に車で送ってもらいました。／
The trains and buses had all stopped, so a friend drove me there.
source_file: 初级下/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第23课.md

title: あれ？
body_lines: This is an interjection uttered when surprised or puzzled, read with rising intonation. Equivalent to "huh?", "eh?"
source_file: 初级下/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第23课.md

title: Verb potential form
body_lines: The verb potential form expresses "can (do something)". The "can" expressed by the Japanese potential form
is close to "can" in English, and likewise expresses two meanings: (1) someone has a certain
ability, or (2) the conditions for doing something are met.
The conjugation rules for the verb potential form are as follows:
Type I verbs: change the final u-row kana to the corresponding e-row kana, then add る.
For example:
返す：かえす→せ＋る＝返せる
書く：かく→け＋る＝書ける
泳ぐ：およぐ→げ＋る＝泳げる
待つ：まつ→て＋る＝待てる
読む：よむ→め＋る＝読める
遊ぶ：あそぶ→べ＋る＝遊べる
送る：おくる→れ＋る＝送れる
Type II verbs: drop the final kana る, then add られる. For example:
辞める：やめる＋られる＝辞められる
寝る：ねる＋られる＝寝られる
Group III (irregular) verbs:
① Suru-verb: change する to できる. That is:
する：する→できる
勉強する：勉強する→できる＝勉強できる
② Kuru-verb: change 来る to 来, then add られる. That is:
来る：くる→来＋られる＝来られる
When using the potential form of a transitive verb, note that the particle を that originally marked
the object is usually changed to が. For example:
私は辛いものを食べません。／I don't eat spicy food.
⇒私は辛いものが食べられません。／I can't eat spicy food.
Also, in recent years young Japanese often drop the ら from the potential forms of type II verbs and the type III verb 来る;
this is quite common in informal spoken language and is called
"ra-dropping words" (ら抜き言葉) in Japanese. For example:
⇒私は辛いものが食べ（ら）れません。／I can't eat spicy food.
⇒ 私 は明日授業 があるので、来（ら）れません。／I have class tomorrow, so I can't come.
① A：明日のパーティーに来られますか。／Can you come to tomorrow's party?
B：はい、行けると思います。／Yes, I think I can go.
② 市場で新鮮な魚が買えます。／You can buy fresh fish at the market.
③ まだ完全に回復していないので、退院できません。／Because (I) haven't fully recovered yet,
I can't be discharged from the hospital.
④ この辺りに、どこかおいしいランチが食べられるところはあります
か。／Is there a place nearby where (we) can get a good lunch?
source_file: 初级下/15.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第24课.md

title: 〜ところだ。
body_lines: As a concrete noun, ところ can be written with the kanji 所 and mainly denotes a place. ところ
can also be used as a formal noun after various affirmative forms of verbs, followed by the copula だ, to ex-
press the stage the action is at.
a．V るところだ。
The dictionary form followed by ところだ indicates that the action is about to begin at the moment of speaking. Can
be translated as "(just) about to ...". It is often paired with time adverbs such as 今, ちょうど, これから.
① 昼ごはんを買いに行くところです。／(I'm) just about to go buy lunch.
② A：もうみなさんに資 料 を配りましたか。／Have you already handed out the materials
to everyone?
B：いえ、これから配るところです。／No, I'm about to hand them out.
b. V ているところだ。
The verb ている form followed by ところだ indicates that the action is in progress at the moment of speaking. Equivalent
to "right now doing ..." in English. Often paired with 今, ちょうど,
③ A： 出席者の人数、もうわかりましたか。／Do you already know the number of attendees?
B：今、調べているところです。／I'm looking into it right now.
④ ちょうど今、テーマを考えているところです。何かいいアイディア
はありますか。／I'm just thinking of a topic right now. Any good ideas?
c. V たところだ。
The verb ta-form followed by ところだ indicates that the action has just finished at the moment of speaking. Can
be translated as "have just ...". It can be paired with time adverbs like 今, たったいま.
⑤ 今、会場に着いたところです。／(I) just arrived at the venue.
⑥ たったいま連絡が入ったところです。／(I) just now got (their) message.
source_file: 初级下/15.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第24课.md

title: V たばかりだ。
body_lines: The verb ta-form followed by ばかり and then the copula だ expresses that the action happened
only a short while ago. Equivalent to "just ...".
① もう忘れたのですか。習ったばかりですよ。／Have you forgotten already? We just
learned it.
② 日本に来たばかりで、まだ敬語を上手に使うことができません。／
I've just come to Japan, so I can't use honorifics well yet.
③ まだインターンに来たばかりなので、いつもコンビニのお弁当で済
ませています。／I just started the internship, so I always make do with a convenience-store bento
(outside).
④ うちには生まれたばかりの子猫が３匹います。／We have 3 newborn kit-
tens at home.
source_file: 初级下/15.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第24课.md

title: N でも＜example＞
body_lines: The particle "でも" follows a noun or particles such as "に" or "と"; when proposing something to the listener, it is used to
offer one example for the listener to consider. This usage is mild and polite, and generally does not need to be translated.
① ちょっとコーヒーでも飲みませんか。／Would you like to have some coffee (or something)?
② わたしのでも使いますか。／Would you like to use mine?
③ 明日の夜、いっしょに映画でも見ますか。／Shall we watch a movie (or some-
thing) together tomorrow night?
④ いっしょにステーキでも食べに行きますか。／Shall we go out for steak or something together?
source_file: 初级下/15.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第24课.md

title: N で <Limitation (quantity)>
body_lines: The particle "で" follows a quantity word or a question word about quantity, and expresses a limitation on quantity.
① 会社から5分で行けます。／You can get there in 5 minutes from the office.
② この車は２００万円では買えませんよ。／You can't buy this car for 2 mil-
lion yen.
③ ここの近くに国産 牛 のローストビーフが千円で食べられるお店が
あるんです。／There is a restaurant near here where you can eat roast beef made with domestic beef for 1,000 yen.
source_file: 初级下/15.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第24课.md

title: （N に）V てほしい / V ないでほしい
body_lines: When the te-form of a verb is followed by "てほしい", it expresses the speaker's wish for the listener or someone else to do something; when the
nai-form is followed by "ないでほしい", it expresses the speaker's wish that the other person not do something. If you need to specify
whom you wish to do (or not do) the action, mark the agent of the action with the particle "に".
① やることがいっぱいあるので、誰かに手伝ってほしいんです。／I have a lot to do, so I'd like someone to help me.
② 子供たちに約束を守ってほしい。／I hope the children will keep their promise.
③ 大事なイベントなので、遅刻しないでほしい。／It's an important event, so I hope
you won't be late.
④ 勝手にスマホを見ないでほしい。／I don't want you to look at my
phone without permission.
When the speaker hopes for a certain state or phenomenon to come about, the subject involved is marked with "が".
In this case, the predicate verb is usually a non-volitional intransitive verb.
⑤ 夏休みが終わらないでほしい。／I hope summer vacation doesn't end.
⑥ お金がない！早く 給 料日が来てほしい。／I'm broke! I hope payday
comes soon.
source_file: 初级下/15.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第24课.md

title: 〜みたいだ＜conjecture＞
body_lines: Pattern: V plain form + みたいだ。
A (i-adjective) plain form + みたいだ。
Ⅰ
※A (na-adjective) plain form (〜だ) + みたいだ。
Ⅱ
※N plain form (〜だ) + みたいだ。
When a plain-form sentence (or a noun / na-adjective stem) is followed by "みたいだ", it expresses the speaker's conjecture. This
conjecture is usually based on the speaker's direct experience or feeling. It is mostly used in spoken language. It can be translated as "it seems...",
"it appears...", etc.
① あの 2人は最近あまり話さない。別れたみたいだ。／Those two haven't been talking
much lately. It seems they've broken up.
② 昨日から熱があります。風邪を引いたみたいです。／I've had a fever since yesterday.
It seems I've caught a cold.
③ A:試験はいつですか。／When is the exam?
B:来月みたいですよ。／It seems to be next month.
④ 中村さんは彼氏ができたみたいですよ。／It seems Nakamura has got a boyfriend.
source_file: 初级下/15.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第24课.md

title: 言っていた <Reporting>
body_lines: When reporting what a third person said, the form "言っていた" is often used. The reported content can also be marked with the particle "と" before "言っ
ていた".
① この前、店長が言っていました。／The store manager said so the other day.
② 私たちで行きましょうか。王さんは行かないと言っていましたから。
／Let's go by ourselves. Xiao Wang said he's not going.
③ A:部長は何と言っていましたか。／What did the department manager say?
B:すこし遅れるから、先に始めてくださいと言っていました。／He said he'd be a little late and told us to start without him.
source_file: 初级下/15.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第24课.md

title: N ではなく（て）
body_lines: When a noun is followed by "ではなく（て）", it negates the content preceding "ではなく（て）" and
adds the correct content after it. It can be translated as "not..., but...". "ではなく" is mostly used
in written form, while "ではなくて" or "じゃなくて" is mostly used in spoken language.
① この前いっしょに食べた 料理は和食 じゃなくて、韓国料理だっ
たんだよ。／What we ate together the other day wasn't Japanese food, it was Korean food.
② この前、山田さんといっしょに来た人は、山田さんの恋人ではなく
て、 妹 さんでした。／The person who came with Yamada the other day wasn't his girlfriend, but his
younger sister.
③ 弁当は日本特有の文化ではなく、世界中どこにでもある。／Bento is not a cul-
ture unique to Japan; it exists everywhere in the world.
source_file: 初级下/17.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第25课.md

title: N である
body_lines: "である" follows a noun to form the predicate of a noun-predicate sentence. It is similar to "です" and "だ".
However, "です" and "だ" are mostly used in spoken language, while "である" is used in plain-form written language. "である" also has a four-
quadrant conjugation, as follows:
Table 25: "Nである" four-quadrant table
Present/
Nである。 Nではない。
Future
Past  Nであった。 Nではなかった。
① 東京は日本の首都である。／Tokyo is the capital of Japan.
② 信頼は大切である。／Trust is important.
source_file: 初级下/17.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第25课.md

title: 〜からだ。＜cause; reason＞
body_lines: When a plain-form sentence is followed by "からだ", it gives a reason; it can be translated as "it is because...". It can be rendered as
"The reason... is because...". Its negative form is "〜からではない", meaning "it is not because...
① けがをして 休学しました。事故に遭ったからです。／I took a leave of absence from school because of
an injury. It was because I had an accident.
② 彼は試験に落ちました。まじめに勉強しなかったからじゃなくて、
病気で休学したからです。／He didn't pass. It wasn't because he didn't study hard,
but because he took a leave of absence due to illness.
③ A:この新商品、ぜんぜん売れませんね。／This new product just isn't selling at all, is it?
B:まだ誰も知らないからだと思いますよ。／I think it's because no one
knows about it yet.
source_file: 初级下/17.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第25课.md

title: N にとって
body_lines: "にとって" usually follows a noun referring to a person or organization, and expresses an evaluation from the stand-
point or perspective of that person or organization. It can be translated as "for..." or "as far as... is concerned".
① 現代人にとって、スマホは生活の一部です。／For modern people, smart-
phones are a part of life.
② 私にとって、日本語学習はとても楽しい。／For me, studying Japanese is
a lot of fun.
③ シンプルなランチボックス文化で育った外国人にとって、日本の弁
当は、いろいろと 興味深いポイントがある。／For foreigners who grew up in a
simple lunchbox culture, Japanese bento has many fascinating points.
source_file: 初级下/17.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第25课.md

title: 〜という N
body_lines: When you need to refer to a person or thing that you or the listener are not familiar with, you can use "という" to intro-
duce it. It can be translated as "(a N) called...".
① 日本には、キャラ弁という弁当もある。／In Japan, there is also a bento called "chara-
ben" (character bento).
② 葛飾北斎という人を聞いたことがありますか。／Have you heard of someone called
Katsushika Hokusai?
③ これはなんという花ですか。／What is this flower called?
Besides the use of a noun followed by "という N", Japanese also allows a sentence followed by "という N"
to explain the specific content of the noun N. For example:
④ 冷たいお弁当は好きじゃないという声もあります。／There are also voices saying
that they don't like cold bento.
source_file: 初级下/17.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第25课.md

title: Question word + でも
body_lines: When a question word is followed by "でも", it expresses that the part indicated by the question word applies to any element, and the statement
holds true in all cases. It can be translated as "no matter..." or "any...".
① どんな時でも 暖 かいお弁当が食べたいです。／I want to eat a warm bento
at any time.
② どんな仕事でもまじめにやらなければなりません。／No matter what job it is,
you have to do it seriously.
③ 地震はいつでも、どこでも起こる可能性があります。／Earthquakes can happen
anytime, anywhere.
④ 中華料理なら何でも好きです。／I like any kind of Chinese food.
source_file: 初级下/17.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第25课.md

title: 〜ようだ。＜conjecture＞
body_lines: Pattern: V/A attributive form + ようだ。
N の+ようだ。
Earlier we learned "〜みたいだ" for expressing conjecture. A noun (when attached to a noun, "noun + の") or the
attributive form of an inflecting word followed by "ようだ" can also express conjecture; it can be translated as "probably...", "it seems
...", etc. Like "〜みたいだ", "〜ようだ" expresses the speaker's inference based on their own impres-
sions or feelings. "〜ようだ" can also be used in written language or more formal situations, whereas "〜
みたいだ" is generally used more in spoken language.
① 中国人は日本の冷たい弁当があまり好きではないようだ。／It seems that
Chinese people don't like cold Japanese bento very much.
② もうそろそろ時間のようなので、今日はこれで終わります。／It seems to be about time, so let's call it a day.
③ 田中さんは最近忙 しいようですよ。食事会に誘っても来てくれま
せん。／Tanaka seems busy lately. Even when I invite him to dinner, he won't come.
④ 先生は怒っているようでした。／The teacher seemed angry.
source_file: 初级下/17.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第25课.md

title: N のようだ。 ＜metaphor＞
body_lines: "Noun + の" followed by "ようだ" is used for metaphor, equivalent to "like...". It is often paired with adverbs
such as "まるで" or "いかにも", and can be translated as "just like...".
① 日本のお弁当は美 しくて、まるで芸術品のようです。／Japanese bento are beauti-
ful, just like works of art.
② 中村さんはやさしくて、李さんにとってお姉さんのようです。／Nakamura is kind, and to Li, she is like an older sister.
③ この一週間は毎日残業 だったので、洗濯物がもう山のようです。
／I worked overtime every day this week, so the laundry is already piled up like a mountain.
source_file: 初级下/17.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第25课.md

title: こと <Formal noun>
body_lines: Besides being used as an ordinary noun meaning "thing/matter", "こと" can also serve as a "formal noun":
when attached after the attributive form of an inflecting word, it functions to nominalize that word within the sentence. The formal noun
"こと" cannot serve as a sentence component on its own; it mainly performs a grammatical function in the sentence and is also often used
in certain fixed grammatical patterns. Other formal nouns commonly used in Japanese include "の" and "もの".
① 私の夢は、医者になることです。／My dream is to become a doctor.
② 弁当全体のバランスを見ながら、盛り付けや味付けを 考 えて作る
ことは、まさに日本特有の文化の一つである。／Looking at the overall
balance of the bento while thinking about how to arrange and season it — this is truly one of Japan's unique cultural traits.
source_file: 初级下/17.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第25课.md

title: 〜すぎる <Excess>
body_lines: Pattern: V masu-stem + すぎる
Aい＋すぎる
Ⅰ
A だ＋すぎる
Ⅱ
A verb masu-stem, an i-adjective with the final "い" removed, or a na-adjective stem followed by "すぎる" expresses that
an action, behavior, or state exceeds the normal degree or range. It can be translated as "too..." or "excessively...".
① 仕事が多すぎて、来 週までには終わらないかもしれない。／There's too much work;
I might not finish it by next week.
② この辺りはにぎやかすぎて、勉強にはよくない。／This area is too lively,
which is not good for studying.
③ 頭が痛いのは、昨夜お酒を飲みすぎたからだと思う。／The reason my head hurts,
I think, is that I drank too much last night.
source_file: 初级下/17.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第25课.md

title: -ba form <conditional form of verbs and adjectives>
category: conditional form of verbs and adjectives
body_lines: Both verbs and adjectives can take the -ba conditional form (also called the provisional form), meaning "if..."
The rules for forming the -ba form of verbs are as follows:
Group I (godan) verbs:
Change the final u-dan kana of the verb to the corresponding e-dan kana, then add "ば". For example:
休む：やすむ→め＋ば＝休めば
行く：いく→け＋ば＝行けば
Group II (ichidan) verbs:
Change the final kana "る" of the verb to "れ", then add "ば". For example:
調べる：しらべる→れ＋ば＝調べれば
Group III (irregular) verbs:
① Suru-verbs: change the final "る" to "れ", then add "ば". That is:
する：する→れ＋ば＝すれば
勉強する：勉強する→れ＋ば＝勉強すれば
② Kuru-verb: change the final "る" to "れ", then add "ば". That is:
来る：くる→くれ＋ば＝来れば
① ネットで調べれば、必要な情報は何でも手に入ります。／If you look it up online,
you can get any information you need.
② 軽い風邪は、ゆっくり休めば治りますよ。／A slight cold will get better if you rest well.
③ 今すぐ電車で行けば、まだ間に合いますよ。／If you go by train right now,
you'll still make it in time.
The rules for forming the -ba form of adjectives are as follows:
I-adjectives: change the final "い" to "ければ".
高い：高い→高ければ
ない：ない→なければ
いい：よい→よければ
※ Note: when the i-adjective "いい" takes "ば", first change "いい" to "よい",
giving "よければ".
Na-adjectives: attach "ならば" to the stem; in modern Japanese the "ば" is usually omitted, leaving just "な
元気：元気→元気なら（ば）
④ 安ければ買いたいけど、安くなければ買わない。／If it's cheap I want to buy it;
if it's not cheap, I won't buy it.
⑤ 作り方が簡単なら、私も作る。／If the recipe is simple, I'll make it too.
When the negative form of a verb (V ない) is made conditional, it follows the adjective conjugation rule, that is:
V ない：Vない→V なければ
⑥ 今すぐ行かなければ、間に合わない。／If we don't go right now,
we won't make it.
source_file: 中级上/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第26课.md

title: 〜たり〜たりする <alternation; listing: たり-1>
body_lines: Replace the "た" of the verb ta-form / i-adjective ta-form with "たり", and attach "だったり" to na-adjectives/
nouns, forming "〜たり〜たりする". It expresses several actions or states alternating within the same period,
or an action or state occurring repeatedly. Two words of opposite meaning can also take "たり"
to show an action repeating back and forth (as in example ②).
① 中村さんはイギリスに行った時、ずっとみんなでいっしょに移動し
たり、見学したりしていたんですか。／Nakamura, when you were in England, did you always go around
with the group, visiting places together?
② 子どもたちがドアを開けたり閉めたりして遊んでいます。／They played, opening and closing the door over and over.
③ この頃、雨が降ったり、強い風が吹いたりして、寒い日が続いてい
ます。／These days it's been raining and blowing hard — cold every day.
④ 部活は月曜日だったり、水曜日だったりして、決まっていません。
／Club activities are sometimes on Monday, sometimes on Wednesday — it's not fixed.
source_file: 中级上/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第26课.md

title: 〜たり〜たりする ＜example: tari-2＞
body_lines: "〜たり〜たりする" can also be used to give examples, picking out two or three representative cases
from several things or actions. In modern Japanese it is more common to list just one example, so it often
appears as "〜たりする". It can be translated as "...and things like that" or "...or something".
The conjugation is the same as the grammar above.
① 道に迷ったりしなかったんですか。／Didn't you get lost or anything?
② ネットがなかった時代には、『地球の歩き方』を手に持って旅にto go out; to leave; to come out
たりしていましたよね。／When there was no internet, we used to travel with a copy of
"How to Walk the Earth" in hand.
③ 昨日は資料を届けに外出したりしていたので、ほとんど席にいま
せんでした。／Yesterday I was out delivering documents and such, so I was hardly at my desk.
source_file: 中级上/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第26课.md

title: V てある <resulting state of an object>
body_lines: A transitive verb followed by "てある" mainly expresses that after someone has deliberately done something,
the resulting state continues to exist. It can be translated as "(something) has been ...-ed (and remains so)".
With "V てある", the verb is usually a volitional transitive verb, and its object is marked with "が" instead.
a. 壁にポスターが貼ってあります。／There is a poster (put up) on the wall.
b. ポスターを壁に貼りました。／(Someone) put the poster up on the wall.
Compared with sentence b, sentence a emphasizes the state in which the poster remains on the wall
after having been put up.
① A：この辞書、だれのですか。／Whose dictionary is this?
B：林さんのだと思いますよ。表紙に名前が書いてありますから。
／I think it's Kobayashi's. There's a name written on the cover.
② この件について課 長にはすでに報告してあります。／Regarding this matter,
I have already reported it to the section chief.
③ そういえば、うちの本棚にもそのガイドブックが置いてありますよ。
／Come to think of it, that travel guide is sitting on my bookshelf at home too.
source_file: 中级上/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第26课.md

title: V るように＜purpose＞
body_lines: Pattern: V る + ように、〜
V ない+ように、〜
The dictionary form or nai-form of a verb followed by "ように" forms a purpose clause, expressing that one does
(or doesn't do) something so that a certain state comes about; it can be translated as "so that...".
The main clause that follows generally expresses the means or action taken to achieve that purpose.
Note that the verb before "ように" is usually a non-volitional verb such as "なる" or "できる",
or a weakly volitional form such as the potential or negative form.
① 家族といっしょに晩ご飯が食べられるように、いつも夕方6時に退
社します。／So that I can have dinner with my family, I always leave work at 6 p.m.
② 後ろの席の人にも見えるように、字を大きくしました。／So that people in the back seats
can see too, I wrote the characters bigger.
③ 明日寝坊しないように、今夜早く寝ましょう。／So that we don't oversleep tomorrow,
let's go to bed early tonight.
④ ネットがなかった時代には、道に迷わないように、『地球の歩き方』
を手に持って旅行していました。／In the days before the internet, so as not to get lost,
people traveled with "How to Walk the Earth" in hand.
source_file: 中级上/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第26课.md

title: 〜そうだ <appearance>
body_lines: Pattern: V ます stem + そうだ.
Aい+そうだ。
Ⅰ
A だ+そうだ。
Ⅱ
An adjective stem or the masu-stem of a verb followed by "そうだ" expresses the speaker's conjecture
based on appearance or past experience. Equivalent to "looks like..." or "seems..." in English.
① あの人はいつも寂しそうです。／That person always looks lonely.
② このテーマなら、すぐに論文が書けそうですね。／With this topic,
it looks like the paper could be written right away.
③ このテーブルは足が太くて、丈夫そうです。／This table has thick legs;
it looks sturdy.
"そうだ" can also modify a noun in the form "〜そうな", or modify a verb/adjective
in the form "〜そうに". For example:
④ あの子は大事そうに人形 を引き出しにしまった。／The child carefully put the doll away in the drawer, as if it were precious.
It introduced the history of travel destinations, local food, and even listed
⑤ 旅先の歴史や現地のグルメ情報を紹介したり、 宿泊施設の電話
番号も載せたりしていて、役に立ちそうな 情報がたくさん書いて
ありました。／It also had inn phone numbers printed — full of useful-looking information.
Also, the adjectives "いい" and "ない" take "そうだ" in the forms "よさ
そうだ" and "なさそうだ" respectively. For example:
⑥ どうかしましたか。あまり元気がなさそうですね。／Is something wrong?
You don't look very well.
⑦ この子は体が丈 夫そうではない。／この子は体が丈夫ではなさ
そうだ。／This child doesn't look very strong.
source_file: 中级上/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第26课.md

title: —切る
body_lines: The masu-stem of a verb followed by "切る" forms a compound verb expressing the thorough completion
of the action (as in examples ①②), or that an action or state has reached its limit (as in examples ③④).
① あの長編小説はとてもおもしろくて、一週間かけて読み切った。
／That long novel was so interesting I finished it in a week.
② 彼女が作ってくれた 料理は美味しいけど、 1人じゃ全部食べ切れ
ません。／Her cooking is delicious, but I can't finish it all by myself.
③ 最近毎日残業 しているので、疲れ切っています。／I've been doing overtime every day lately,
so I'm completely exhausted.
④ どうしてそんなわかりきったことを言わなきゃいけないんですか。
／Why must one spell out something so obvious?
Expression Notes
"そういえば" is used when something comes to mind mid-conversation, or to change the topic.
It is often used to bring up a shared topic one has just recalled or something one has experienced.
It can be translated as "come to think of it..." or "now that you mention it...".
① A：そういえば、いつか富士山に登りたいと言っていましたよね。
／Come to think of it, you said you wanted to climb Mt. Fuji sometime.
B：うん。／Yeah.
② A：そういえば、知ってる？／Hey, come to think of it, did you know?
B：なに？／What?
source_file: 中级上/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第26课.md

title: 〜といっても、〜
body_lines: Pattern: plain sentence / noun だ ＋といっても、〜
A noun or the plain form of a verb/adjective followed by "といっても" forms a concessive clause. The main
clause qualifies or corrects the content of the subordinate clause, expressing that in reality the thing does not
reach the degree the clause describes — "although...; even though...; ...but really...".
① ホテルの近くに公園があります。公園といっても、小さなお庭です。
／There's a park near the hotel. Though calling it a park, it's really just a small courtyard.
② 学費は高いといっても、払えないほど高くありません。／Although tuition is
expensive, it's not so expensive that you can't pay it.
③ アフリカで暮らしたことがあるといっても、実は３ヶ月だけなんです。
／Although I lived in Africa, it was actually only three months.
source_file: 中级上/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第27课.md

title: 〜か〜
body_lines: In Japanese, a plain-form question ending with the particle "か" can be embedded in another sentence,
becoming part of it. Note that a noun or na-adjective stem can directly take the question particle "か".
① いつ奨学金をもらったか覚えていますか。／Do you remember when you
received the scholarship?
② 地震の時、どこへ避難するか教えてください。／Please tell me where to evacuate
in the event of an earthquake.
③ どんなスポーツが得意か書いてください。／Please write down which sports
you are good at.
source_file: 中级上/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第27课.md

title: V るようになる <change>
body_lines: The dictionary form of a verb followed by "ようになる" expresses change: gaining an ability (from being unable
to do something to being able to do it), or acquiring a habit (from not doing something to doing it). For example:
① 積極的に自分から意見が言えるようになった。／(I've become) able to
express my own opinions proactively.
② 隣 の子供は最近きちんとあいさつするようになった。／The neighbor's kid
has started greeting people properly lately.
③ 日本語が話せるようになりました。／I've become able to speak Japanese.
source_file: 中级上/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第27课.md

title: 〜し、〜 <listing; coordination>
body_lines: Pattern: plain sentence + し、〜
The particle "し" attaches to a clause: two or more "し"-clauses can be coordinated to list reasons;
or a single "し"-clause can cite just one reason among several.
Translate as "both...and...", "what's more...".
① 今日は雨だし、風も強いし、約束をキャンセルしましょうか。／today
It's raining, and the wind is strong too — let's cancel our date.
② このアパートは静かだし、日当たりもいいし、とても快適だ。／This apartment
is quiet, and it gets good sunlight — very comfortable.
③ 今日はボーナスをもらったし、高級 レストランでおいしいものを食べ
ましょう。／I got my bonus today, so let's go eat something nice at a fancy restaurant.
source_file: 中级上/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第27课.md

title: 〜に対する・〜に対して
body_lines: "〜に対する・〜に対して" usually attaches to nouns referring to people or abstract things, indicating
the target of an action, feeling, or attitude — "toward(s)...; regarding...". "〜に対する" can modify a noun;
to modify a predicate, use the form "〜に対して + predicate".
① 林 さんに対する尊敬心はいつごろからのものですか。／Since when have you
looked up to Mr. Lin?
② マスコミに対して、「ノーコメント」を繰り返した。／To the media, he repeatedly
said "no comment".
③ この学校の先生たちは、学生に対して本当にやさしいです。／The teachers at this school
are truly kind to their students.
source_file: 中级上/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第27课.md

title: V ばいい
body_lines: With a purpose or reason as premise, the conditional "V ば" followed by the adjective "いい" can be used
to give advice or state a suitable method or means — "you can...; ...will do; just..."
① その仕事が嫌なら、やめればいい。／If you don't like the job, just quit.
② この町の歴史なら、山田さんに聞けばいいですよ。／If it's about this town's history,
you can ask Yamada.
③ A：頭が痛い…／My head hurts...
B：この薬を飲めばいいよ。すぐ治るよ。／Take this medicine. You'll get better
right away.
source_file: 中级上/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第27课.md

title: V てみる
body_lines: The te-form of a verb followed by "てみる" expresses trying something out — "try ...-ing".
① 一度日本に行ってみたいです。／I want to go to Japan at least once.
② 留学 のことはもう一度親と相談してみます。／About studying abroad, I'll try discussing it once more
with my parents.
③ わからないことは、あの人に聞いてみればいいです。／If there's something you don't understand,
try asking that person.
source_file: 中级上/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第27课.md

title: ために＜purpose＞
body_lines: Pattern: N の + ために
V る+ために
"Noun + の" or the dictionary form of a verb followed by "ために" expresses purpose. When "ために"
expresses purpose, the subjects of the two clauses must be the same, and the action in the main clause
should be a volitional verb aimed at achieving that purpose.
① 日本の伝統文化を理解するために、茶道を習いました。／
To learn about Japan's traditional culture, I studied the tea ceremony.
② 転職のために、いろいろ面接を受けた。／To change jobs, I went to various interviews.
③ 家を買うために、朝から晩まで働く。／To buy a house, I work from morning to night.
source_file: 中级上/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第27课.md

title: 〜ところ、〜
body_lines: Pattern: V る／V ている／V た＋ところ、〜
"ところ" follows the plain verb form, "V ている", or "V た", highlighting the point in time within the
course of the action — with the nuance that the main clause's event interrupts the ongoing state of the subordinate
clause. Similar to the "V る／Vている／Vた＋ところだ" learned in Lesson 24, "V るところ" marks a point just
before the action happens, "V ているところ" a point while it is in progress, and "V たところ" a point just
after it has happened. Depending on the verb in the main clause, particles such as "に、を、へ、で"
can follow "V る／V ている／V た＋ところ".
① ずっと楽しみにしていたドラマが始まったところ（に）、電話がかかっ
てきた。／Just as the drama I'd been looking forward to was starting, a phone call came in.
② その試合はもう少しで終わるところ（で）、雨で中止になった。／match; game; competition
It was just about to end when, at that very moment, it was called off due to rain.
③ ようやく工事が始まったところ（に）、台風が来た。／Construction had finally just begun,
when the typhoon came.
source_file: 中级上/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第27课.md

title: 〜そうにもない
body_lines: Pattern: V ます stem ＋そうにもない
Lesson 26 covered "〜そうだ" for appearance. The negative form of the masu-stem + "そうだ" is
"〜そうにもない"; the "に" and "も" can each be omitted, giving "〜そうにない" or "〜そうもない".
① このプロジェクトは 1人の 力 では完成できそうにない。／This project
cannot be completed by one person's strength alone.
② 全く勉強していないので、合格しそうもない。／I haven't studied at all, so there's
no way I'll pass.
③ この問題は 難 しすぎて、僕にはわかりそうもない。／This problem is too hard;
there's no way I can understand it.
source_file: 中级上/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第27课.md

title: わ <sentence-final particle>
body_lines: The sentence-final particle "わ" expresses mild emotion or surprise. The "わ" in example ① is usually
spoken with a rising intonation, mostly by older women; the "わ" in example ② can also be used by men,
but with a falling intonation.
① あら、きれいな人だわ。／Oh my, what a beautiful person.
② ほんと、助かるわ。／Really, that's a big help.
source_file: 中级上/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第27课.md

title: 〜と、〜 <condition>
body_lines: Pattern: N だ + と、〜
Aい+と、〜
Ⅰ
A だ+と、〜
Ⅱ
V る+と、〜
The dictionary form of a verb or i-adjective, or "noun/na-adjective + だ", followed by "と" forms a
conditional sentence expressing that whenever the former holds, the latter invariably follows.
Translate as "when... (then)...", "if..., ...". This pattern is also often used when giving directions, as in ④.
① スイッチを入れると、部屋が明るくなります。／When you flip the switch, the room
lights up.
② 貧乏だと、就 職も結婚もできない。／If you're poor, you can neither find a job
nor get married.
③ 気温が低いと、桜が咲きません。／If the temperature is low, the cherry blossoms won't bloom.
④ まっすぐ行くと、左 手に大きな駐車場が見えます。／Go straight, and on your left
you'll see a large parking lot.
source_file: 中级上/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第28课.md

title: V ておく
body_lines: The te-form of a verb followed by "ておく" expresses doing something in advance for a certain need,
or keeping a certain state as a temporary measure — "...in advance; ...and leave it (as is)". In speech,
"V ておく" often contracts to "V とく".
① 明日出かけるので、車を充電しておいてください。／Because I'm going out tomorrow,
Before leaving, please charge the car in advance.
② 次回はこの文章 の内容をいっしょに翻訳しますので、今回はまず読
んでおきましょう。／Next time we'll translate the content of this text together, so this time
let's read it through first.
③ コピー用紙がないから、買っておいてください。／We're out of copy paper,
so please buy some (in advance).
