source_file: 中级上/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第28课.md

title: 〜ことになる <outcome; arrangement>
body_lines: Pattern: V る＋ことになる
V ない＋ことになる
The dictionary or nai-form of a verb followed by "ことになる" expresses a result arising from the natural
course of events; the form "V る／V ない＋ことになっている" expresses an established rule or arrangement, e.g.:
① 2年後には帰国することになると思います。／I think I'll end up returning home in two years.
② 来年の4月に日本に 留学することになりました。／It's been decided that I'll go study in Japan
in April next year.
③ 工場見学に行く人は、20日までに申請のメールを出すことになって
います。／Those going on the factory tour are required to send the application email by the 20th.
source_file: 中级上/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第28课.md

title: N まで ＜degree＞
body_lines: We learned that the particle "まで" follows a time or place to mark a range. "まで" can also follow
nouns other than time/place to express extent, often with the speaker's surprise — "even...; to the point of...".
① 由加ちゃんまで花粉 症になった。／Even Yuka has come down with hay fever.
② 内定をもらったし、彼女もできた。さらに、宝くじまで当たった！／
I got a job offer and a girlfriend. And on top of that, I even won the lottery!
③ 近頃、子供だけでなく、大人まで漫画を読んでいる。／These days, not only children
but even adults read manga.
source_file: 中级上/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第28课.md

title: 〜のに ＜contrast＞
body_lines: Pattern: N な + のに
V/A attributive form + のに
"Noun + な" or the attributive form of a verb/adjective followed by the particle "のに" forms an adversative
compound sentence: the premise or cause in the first clause does not lead to the expected result in the second.
The speaker often sounds surprised or dissatisfied. Translate as "...yet...; although...". Both clauses of "のに"
are usually established facts; in particular, the second clause cannot be a command, request, or wish.
① まだ4月なのに、夏よりも暑い。／It's only April, yet it's hotter than summer.
② 今日は大雪が降っているのに、朝から授業がある。／It's snowing heavily today, yet
we have classes from the morning.
③ もう薬を飲んでいるのに、体調はぜんぜん良くならない。／I'm already taking medicine,
yet I'm not getting any better.
source_file: 中级上/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第28课.md

title: 〜らしい <hearsay>
body_lines: "らしい" attaches to the plain form of a verb/adjective (na-adjectives drop だ) or a noun, expressing hearsay
or conjecture based on objective grounds — "it seems...; I hear...; apparently...". The objective source can be
marked with "〜によると" or "聞いたところでは".
① 聞いた 話 では、田中さんは来月仕事を辞めるらしいです。／From what I hear,
Tanaka is apparently quitting his job next month.
② 会長は今日欠席するらしいですよ。さっき連絡が入りました。／It seems the chairman
will be absent today. A notice just came in.
③ あの人は業界ではかなり有名らしい。／That person seems quite famous in the industry.
source_file: 中级上/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第28课.md

title: N だらけ
body_lines: A noun followed by "だらけ" expresses that something is all over a place, in a derogatory sense —
"covered with...; full of...; riddled with...".
① 子供たちは泥だらけになって、遊んでいる。／The children are playing, covered in mud.
② 母：ほら、部屋中 はほこりだらけだよ。掃除しましょうよ。／Look,
the room is covered in dust. Let's clean up.
息子：わかった。／Got it.
③ もう傷だらけなのに、とても大切なものだから、捨てられない。／It's already covered in scratches, but because it's so precious to me, I can't throw it away.
source_file: 中级上/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第28课.md

title: 〜途 中 （に／で）、〜
body_lines: Pattern: N の + 途中（に／で）、〜
V る+途中（に／で）、〜
An action noun + の, or the dictionary form of a verb, followed by "途中（に／で）" expresses that before
the action is completed, something else happens; or that something exists on the way somewhere —
"on the way...; midway through...". The particle "に／で" after "〜途中" can be omitted.
① 会社に行く途中で、急に気分が悪くなって倒れた。／On the way to work,
he suddenly felt sick and collapsed.
② 通学の途中 に、たくさんくしゃみが聞こえた。／On the way to school, I heard
lots of sneezing.
③ 大学に行く途中、高校時代の友達に会った。／On the way to university, I ran into
a friend from high school.
source_file: 中级上/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第28课.md

title: 〜ような気がする
body_lines: Pattern: N の + ような気がする
V/A attributive form + ような気がする
"Noun + の" or an attributive form followed by "ような気がする" is similar to the conjecture "ようだ"
learned earlier. "〜ような" modifies the following noun "気". "気がする" means "to have a feeling",
"to feel somehow". Here "気" can be replaced by "感じ" or "予感".
"〜ような気がする" is often paired with adverbs like "なんとなく" and "何だか".
It corresponds to "I feel like...; I have a feeling that...".
① 何だかもう仕方がないような気がします。／I somehow feel there's nothing more to be done.
② 運動のあと、なんとなく 体 が軽くなったような感じがする。／After exercising,
I somehow feel my body has become lighter.
③ あの人にはどこかで会ったような気がします。／I have a feeling I've met
that person somewhere before.
source_file: 中级上/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第28课.md

title: V た/V ないほうがいい <advice>
body_lines: The ta-form or nai-form of a verb followed by "ほうがいい" expresses advice or recommendation —
"you'd better (do)...; it would be better not to...".
① わからないときは、先生に聞いたほうがいいと思います。／When you don't understand,
I think you'd better ask the teacher.
② 体が弱いんだから、無理をしないほうがいいですよ。／You're weak, so you'd better
not push yourself.
③ あまり濃いコーヒーを飲まないほうがいいです。／It's best not to drink coffee that's too strong.
source_file: 中级上/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第28课.md

title: 〜なんて
body_lines: "なんて" can follow certain words or plain sentences, presenting the content before "なんて" as
presents it as a topic. The content before "なんて" is usually something the listener already knows; the predicate
after "なんて" is usually the speaker's evaluation of it, often with surprise, strong negation, or contempt.
"なんて" is mostly used in spoken language.
① 宝くじに当たったなんて、すごいですね。／(To think you) won the lottery — amazing!
② 野菜なんて、嫌い！／Vegetables? I hate them!
③ あんな人が課長だなんて、信じられない！／(To think) someone like that is a section chief —
I can't believe it!
source_file: 中级上/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第28课.md

title: 〜につれて <as; along with>
body_lines: Pattern: V る＋につれて
N＋につれて
After a noun expressing change (action, phenomenon, etc.) or the dictionary form of a verb, "につれて"
expresses that as the former situation changes or develops, the latter changes or develops accordingly.
Both clauses of "につれて" should be verbs or nouns expressing change. Translate as "as...; along with..."
① 期末テストが近づくにつれて、どんどん不安になる。／As the final exams
draw nearer, I get more and more anxious.
② 大人になるにつれて、好みも変わっていく。／As you become an adult, your tastes
change too.
③ 経済の発展につれて、海外旅行する人も多くなりました。／As the economy
developed, more people started traveling abroad.
source_file: 中级上/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第29课.md

title: V ていく/くる <movement; change>
body_lines: The te-form of a verb followed by "ていく" or "てくる" indicates the direction of movement or change.
I. Movement
"ていく" and "てくる" can follow a movement verb to show the direction of the action, or a stative verb
to show moving while maintaining that state. "V ていく" and "V てくる" can be translated as "...and go"
and "...and come" respectively. "V てくる" can also mean doing something and then coming
back, as in example ③.
① 病院へ行く途中で、お見舞いの花を買っていきましょう。／On the way to the hospital,
let's buy some flowers for our visit.
② この川は富士山から流れてくる。／This river flows down from Mt. Fuji.
③ ちょっと待って。本を持ってくるね。／Hang on. I'll go get the book.
II. Change
A. "V ていく" presents a prospect from now into the future, or the continuation of a developing process
or state — "...on; keep ...-ing; go on ...-ing" (may be left untranslated).
① この事件は継続的に 調査していく必要があります。／This case needs to
be investigated continuously going forward.
② これからもがんばっていきましょう。／Let's keep doing our best
from now on.
B. "V てくる" presents a gradual change from the past or continuation of a state; the form "V てきた"
can also express the strengthening of a feeling or emotion, as in example ① — "...has come to...; ...has started to...".
① １２時を過ぎても 娘 が帰ってこない。なんだか心配になってきた。
／It's past 12 and my daughter still isn't home. I can't help starting to worry.
② 寒くなって、風邪をひく人が多くなってきた。／It's gotten cold, and more people
have started catching colds.
source_file: 中级上/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第29课.md

title: 〜そうだ <hearsay; quotation>
body_lines: A plain sentence followed by "そうだ" expresses hearsay or reported information. The hearsay expressed by
"〜そうだ" cannot be the speaker's own direct inference; it is indirectly heard or reported. The source
can be made explicit with "〜によると", "〜によれば", "〜では", etc.
① 担当者の 話 によれば、新発売の 商品は 1日で売り切れたそうです。
／According to the person in charge, the newly released product sold out in one day.
② 今回の試験の合格率は 5％だったそうだ。／I hear the pass rate for this exam was
③ 予報では、台風は今夜 上陸するそうだ。／According to the forecast, the typhoon will make landfall tonight.
source_file: 中级上/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第29课.md

title: 〜ということだ
body_lines: A plain sentence followed by "ということだ" sums up, paraphrases, or explains the facts stated before.
Such an explanation is mostly the speaker's inference, judgment, or evaluation.
① えっ？山田さんはまだ来ていませんか。つまり、また遅刻したという
ことですね。／Huh? Yamada still isn't here? So that means he's late again.
② 時給８００円というのは、月曜から金曜まで働いても、１ヶ月で１
５万円にもならないということだ。／800 yen an hour — in other words, even working
Monday to Friday, you wouldn't make 150,000 yen a month.
③ 日本の飲食店は全面禁煙です。つまり、お店の中でタバコを吸っては
いけないということです。／Japanese restaurants have gone completely non-smoking. In other words,
you may not smoke inside the establishment.
source_file: 中级上/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第29课.md

title: 〜にかけて
body_lines: "にかけて" follows a noun of time or place to express a range, usually in the form "〜から〜にかけて"
— "from ... to ...". Similar to "〜から〜まで", but "〜から〜にかけて" has no clear boundary,
loosely spanning two points in time or space.
① 今月から来月にかけて仕事を休むつもりです。／I plan to take off from this month
through next month.
② 今夜から明日の早朝 にかけて大雨だそうです。／They say there will be heavy rain from tonight
through early tomorrow morning.
③ 東京から京都にかけてかなり暑くなるでしょう。／It will get pretty hot
from Tokyo to Kyoto.
source_file: 中级上/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第29课.md

title: V る／N ごとに
body_lines: A noun or dictionary-form verb followed by "ごとに" expresses each recurrence of a repeated event,
or every single complete occurrence — "every...; each...".
① この目覚まし時計は５分ごとに鳴る。／This alarm clock rings every 5 minutes.
② 国ごとにそれぞれの文化や 習慣がある。／Every country has its own culture
and customs.
③ 感染予防のために、１時間ごとにエレベーターを消毒する。／To prevent infection,
the elevators are disinfected every hour.
source_file: 中级上/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第29课.md

title: N によって
body_lines: A noun followed by "によって" expresses a basis or grounds for judgment, often used with words
like "違う" — "depending on...; it varies with/by...".
① 人によって、考え方が違う。／Ways of thinking differ from person to person.
② 時によって、やり方を変えたほうがやりやすいかもしれない。／Depending on the occasion,
changing the approach may make it easier to do.
③ 私 はその日の気分によって、服を変えます。／I change my clothes depending on my mood
that day.
source_file: 中级上/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第29课.md

title: N として ＜as; in the capacity of＞
body_lines: A noun followed by "として" expresses the capacity or status in which the subject acts — "as..."
① 今年の 4月から、弁護士として働くことになった。／Starting this April,
I will work as a lawyer.
② 彼女は女優として活躍している。／She is active as an actress.
③ 僕は夫として、そして父として、この家族を大切にしていく。／As a husband, and as a father, I will continue to cherish this family.
As a husband and as a father, I will always cherish this family.
source_file: 中级上/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第29课.md

title: 〜ようにする
body_lines: The dictionary or nai-form of a verb followed by "ようにする" expresses making an effort to do (or not do)
something so as to reach a goal or state. Often paired with adverbs like "できるだけ" and "なるべく" —
"to make a point of...; to try to...".
① 最近太ったから、毎日５キロ走るようにしています。／I've gained weight lately, so I make a point of
running 5 kilometers every day.
② 高校時代は自分から意見を言わないようにしていた。／In high school, I made a point of
not voicing my own opinions.
③ 約束を守るようにしてほしい。／I want you to keep your promises.
④ 甘いものは食べないようにしている。／I make a point of not eating sweets.
source_file: 中级上/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第29课.md

title: 〜ことだ＜advice; warning＞
body_lines: Pattern: V る＋ことだ
V ない＋ことだ
The dictionary or nai-form of a verb followed by "ことだ" indirectly offers advice or a gentle instruction
to the listener. Mostly used in everyday conversation.
① 痩せたいなら、毎日運動することだ。／If you want to lose weight, you should exercise every day.
② いい成績を取りたいなら、勉強 をサボらないことです。／If you want to get good grades, you mustn't slack off on your studies.
③ A：友達を増やしたいけど、どうすればいいですか。／I want to make more friends —
what should I do?
B：サークルに入って違う学部の人と話してみることですよ。／You should join a club
and try talking to people from other departments.
source_file: 中级上/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第29课.md

title: N における・N において
body_lines: A noun followed by "における" or "において" indicates a space, time, range, or field —
"in... (terms of); at...; within...". "N における" can modify a noun; "N において" can precede a predicate.
① 現代社会における環 境問題について研究したい。／I want to research environmental problems
in modern society.
② 人生においては、何事も偶然である。／In life, everything is a matter of chance.
③ 日本における英語教育は問題だらけだ。／English education in Japan is riddled with problems.
source_file: 中级上/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第29课.md

title: 〜て、〜 ＜cause; reason＞
body_lines: Pattern: V te-form + て、〜
Aい→く+て、〜
Ⅰ
A だ+で、〜
Ⅱ
N だ+で、〜
The te-form of a verb or i-adjective followed by "て", or a noun or na-adjective stem followed by "で",
forms a clause expressing a mild cause. The main clause can only state objective facts — not commands,
suggestions, or other volitional expressions. When the negative of a verb takes "て" for a reason,
use the form "V なくて" (as in example ③).
① 工場の近くは汚染がひどくて、変な臭いがする。／The pollution near the factory is terrible,
and there's a strange smell.
② 字が下手で、恥ずかしいです。／My handwriting is bad, so I'm embarrassed.
③ 昨日は夜遅くまで仕事が終わらなくて、大変でした。／Yesterday I couldn't finish work until late at night;
it was rough.
④ 久しぶりに友達に会えて、とても嬉しいです。／I'm so happy I could see a friend
after a long time.
source_file: 中级上/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第30课.md

title: 〜たら、〜 <condition>
body_lines: Pattern: V ta-form + たら、〜
Aい→かったら、〜
Ⅰ
A だ+ったら、〜
Ⅱ
N だ+ったら、〜
"たら" can attach to verbs, nouns, and adjectives, forming a hypothetical conditional —
"if/when... (then)...". In use, the content before "たら" is assumed to have come true, and the latter
clause (main clause) expresses the speaker's inference about the possible result, or a request to the listener.
The latter clause of "〜たら、〜" can also express the speaker's will, instructions, commands, or suggestions.
① わからないことがあったら、何でも聞いて。／If there's anything you don't understand,
ask me anything.
② 仕事がきつかったら、すぐに辞めてしまう若者は多くいる。／Many young people
quit right away if the job is tough.
③ 女の子だったら、「ゆうこ」という名前をつけたい。／If it's a girl, I want to name her “Yuko”.
④ 田中さんが来たら、会議を始めましょう。／When Tanaka arrives, let's start the meeting.
source_file: 中级上/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第30课.md

title: 〜か <choice>
body_lines: Verbs, adjectives, and nouns can all take "か" to select among or list the options before it —
① 夏休みはシンガポールかタイに行きたい。／For summer vacation I want to go to Singapore or Thailand.
② 晩ご飯はお寿司かラーメン、どっちがいい？／For dinner, sushi or ramen —
which is better?
③ バスで行くか、地下鉄で行くか決めよう。／Let's decide whether to go by bus
or by subway.
④ 留学に行くか、就 職 するか、かなり悩んでいる。／Whether to study abroad or get a job —
I'm really torn.
source_file: 中级上/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第30课.md

title: 〜場合（は）、〜
body_lines: Pattern: V/A attributive form + 場合（は）、〜
N の+場合（は）、〜
The attributive form of a verb/adjective, or "noun + の", followed by "場合（は）" picks out one situation
from among the possibilities and states the measure to take or judgment to make should it occur —
"in the case of...; if/when...".
① 来週の休みが1 日の場合は市内で、2日間ある場合は郊外でセミナー
をしましょう。／If next week's break is one day, let's hold the seminar in the city; if it's two days,
in the suburbs.
② 地震が起きた場合は、まず火を消さなければなりません。／If an earthquake occurs,
you must first put out the fire.
③ 階段が困難な場合は、こちらのエレベーターを使ってください。／If stairs are difficult for you, please use this elevator.
④ 熱が続く場合は、病 院に行ったほうがいい。／If the fever persists, you'd better go to the hospital.
source_file: 中级上/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第30课.md

title: V ることにする/V ないことにする <personal decision>
body_lines: The dictionary or nai-form of a verb followed by "ことにする" expresses a personal decision to do something.
① もう眠いから、明日早く起きて宿題をすることにします。／I'm too sleepy,
so I've decided to get up early tomorrow and do my homework.
② 今日からお酒を飲まないことにする！／As of today, I'm giving up alcohol!
③ この冬休みはこれまで学んだ知識を復習することにしました。／This winter vacation
I've decided to review what I've learned so far.
source_file: 中级上/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第30课.md

title: V ることはない
body_lines: The dictionary form of a verb followed by "ことはない" expresses the speaker's view that there is no need
to do the action. This pattern is often used when advising the listener, commonly as "何も〜ことはない"
or "わざわざ〜ことはない".
① 今回の試験は簡単な質問だけだから、何も心配することはありません。
／This exam is just easy questions, so there's no need to worry at all.
② ネットで予約することができるから、わざわざ電話することはない。
／You can book online, so there's no need to go out of your way to call.
③ スマホのアプリはとても便利だから、わざわざ紙の地図を見ることは
ないと思う。／Smartphone apps are so convenient that I don't think you need to bother with a paper map.
source_file: 中级上/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第30课.md

title: 〜のじゃないか（と思う）
body_lines: Pattern: plain sentence ＋のではないか（と思う）
※N だ→な＋のではないか（と思う）
※A だ→な＋のではないか（と思う）
Ⅱ
A plain sentence (for nouns and na-adjectives in the non-past, the final "だ" changes to "な") followed by
"のじゃないか" expresses an uncertain conjecture — "might...?; I wonder if...; perhaps...".
Combined with "と思う", the tone is even softer. In speech, the form
"〜のじゃないか（と思う）" is more common.
① 面接は来月の下 旬 になるんじゃないかな。／The interview will probably be in late
next month, I think.
② ずっと 入院していたら、ホームシックになってしまうんじゃないか
と思って、お見舞いに来ました。／I thought that after such a long hospital stay you might be
getting homesick, so I came to visit.
③ こんなに高い時計を買ってあげるなんて、子供を甘やかしているんじ
ゃないかと思います。／Buying the child such an expensive watch — I wonder if it's
spoiling him a bit too much.
source_file: 中级上/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第30课.md

title: V てみせる＜demonstration＞
body_lines: A verb followed by "てみせる" is used to demonstrate an action to the listener — "(I'll do it) and show you".
"V てみせる" can also express strong determination to prove something to others (as in example ②).
① 実際に作ってみせますね。／I'll actually make it and show you.
② 将来 は絶対に社長になってみせる！／Someday I'll definitely become a company president — I'll show you!
③ ひらがなの書き方がまだよくわからないので、書いてみせてくれませ
んか。／I still don't really know how to write hiragana — could you write it out and show me?
source_file: 中级上/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第30课.md

title: V ていただけますか。 <request>
body_lines: The te-form followed by "ていただけますか" politely asks someone to do something for you.
Here "いただける" is the potential form of "いただく" (to receive). Compared with "V ていた
だけますか", "V ていただけませんか" is even more polite.
① 教えていただけますか。／Could you please teach me?
② 論文を書き終えたので、見ていただけますか。／I've finished my paper — could you
please take a look at it?
③ すぐ着くと連絡が入りましたので、もう少々 待っていただけません
か。／I got word that he'll arrive soon — could you please wait a little longer?
source_file: 中级上/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第30课.md

title: V てもらってもいいですか。 <request>
body_lines: The te-form followed by "てもらってもいいですか" asks someone to do something for you —
"Could I ask you to ...?". "V てもらってもいいですか" is common among young people;
it is less soft and polite than "V ていただけますか", and should not be used to elders
or people of higher age or status.
① 実際にやりながら、教えてもらってもいいですか。／Could you teach me while actually doing it?
② この本を貸してもらってもいい？／Can you lend me this book?
③ あと５分ぐらい待ってもらってもいいですか。／Could you wait about five more minutes?
source_file: 中级上/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第30课.md

title: V るべきだ <should; ought to>
body_lines: The dictionary form of a verb followed by "べきだ" expresses that one must or should do something; translate as "should/must ...".
Its negative form is "べきではない", meaning it is better not to do so; "should not ...".
When "する" takes "べきだ", it can be either "するべきだ" or "すべきだ".
① お年寄りに対して、あんな言葉遣いで話すべきではない。／You shouldn't speak to elderly people
with language like that.
② お年寄りに対して、あんな言い方をするべきではない。／You shouldn't talk to elderly people
in that manner.
③ 大学時代はいろいろな体験をすべきだと思う。／I think you should experience many things
during your university years.
④ 学生は学校のルールを守るべきです。／Students should follow the school rules.
"V るべきだ" can also modify a following noun; when it does, use the form "V るべきN", for example:
⑤ どこか直すべきところはありますか。／Is there anywhere that should be fixed?
⑥ 彼女に言うべきことを全部言った。／I said everything I ought to say to her.
source_file: 中级上/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第31课.md

title: 〜わりに（は）
body_lines: Pattern: V attributive form ＋わりに（は）
A attributive form ＋わりに（は）
Ⅰ
A attributive form ＋わりに（は）
Ⅱ
N＋の＋わりに（は）
The attributive form of a verb or adjective, or "N＋の", followed by "わりに（は）" expresses that the result
in the latter clause does not match what would naturally be expected from the former. Translate as "...yet...", "for..."
① 人生経験が豊かなわりには、人を見る目がない。／For all his rich life experience,
he has no eye for people.
② あまり勉強しなかったわりには、この前のテストの成績はまあまあだ
った。／I didn't study much, yet I did pretty well on the last exam.
③ 昨日の講演会は、思ったわりには人が集まらなかった。／Yesterday's lecture
drew fewer people than expected.
④ 海に近いから、気温が高いわりには、暑く感じないね。／Being near the sea,
it doesn't feel hot for how high the temperature is.
source_file: 中级上/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第31课.md

title: 〜からには、〜
body_lines: Pattern: plain sentence ＋からには、〜
※ N だ→である＋からには、〜
※ A だ→である＋からには、〜
Ⅱ
A plain-style sentence (nouns and na-adjectives drop "だ" and take "である") followed by "からには"
expresses the speaker's judgment based on the situation in the first clause; the latter clause often uses
expressions of conjecture, suggestion, determination, wish, or obligation. Translate as "since...; now that...".
① 代表になって全国大会に出るからには、優勝を目指したい。／Now that I'm going to the national tournament
as a representative, I want to aim for the championship.
② 日本に住むからには、日本語が少し話せた方がいいでしょう。／Since you're living in Japan, you'd better be able to speak some Japanese.
③ 生きているからには、楽しく生きよう。／Since we're alive, let's live happily.
source_file: 中级上/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第31课.md

title: V ないで
body_lines: The nai-form of a verb followed by "で" is the negative continuative form: doing the latter action
without doing the former, or the latter happening instead. Translate as "without ...-ing".
① 5段階評価を使わないで、もっと答えやすい質問にする。／Don't use the 5-point rating scale; replace it with questions that are easier to answer.
② もう疲れたから、観光に行かないで、直接ホテルに帰ろう。／I'm tired already, so let's skip sightseeing
and go straight back to the hotel.
③ 子供が来ないで、親が来た。／The child didn't come; the parents came instead.
④ お風呂に入らないで寝てしまった。／I went to sleep without taking a bath.
source_file: 中级上/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第31课.md

title: 〜なら
body_lines: Pattern: A / A / V plain form ＋なら
Ⅰ Ⅱ
※N だ＋なら
※A だ＋なら
Ⅱ
We learned earlier that a noun followed by "なら" highlights a topic (Lesson 15). Besides nouns,
plain-style sentences can also take "なら" to form a conditional, used to state one's own opinion or judgment
based on what the other person said or the situation at hand. The latter clause of "なら" often uses
expressions of judgment, volition, command, request, or evaluation. Translate as "if..., (then) ...".
① 買い物に行くなら、 醤油も買ってきてもらえる？／If you're going shopping,
could you buy me some soy sauce?
② それを知っているなら、もっと早く教えてほしかった。／If you knew that, I wish you had told me earlier.
③ 親まで反対しているなら、その夢は 諦 めたほうがいいよ。／If even your parents
are against it, you'd better give up that dream.
source_file: 中级上/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第31课.md

title: N に加えて
body_lines: A noun followed by "に加えて" expresses that something else is added on top of that thing or event,
or another event occurs in addition. Mostly used in written language. Translate as "in addition to...; plus...".
① 激しい雨に加えて、強い風も吹いている。／Heavy rain, plus strong wind blowing.
② 日本語に加えて、英語も上手だ。／On top of Japanese, she's good at English too.
③ この地域は、豊かな自然に加えて、歴史的な建物も多く存在します。
／This area has not only rich natural scenery but also many historical buildings.
source_file: 中级上/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第31课.md

title: V やすい・V にくい
body_lines: Pattern: V ます stem ＋やすい
V ます＋にくい
The masu-stem of a verb followed by "やすい" or "にくい" forms a derived adjective meaning the action
is easy or hard to do. For example:
① この辺りはコンビニもスーパーもなくて、とても住みにくいです。／
There is neither a convenience store nor a supermarket nearby, so it's very inconvenient to live here.
② スマホの文字の 表示を大きくしたら、読みやすくなりました。／When I enlarged the text display on my phone, it became easier to read.
③ 先輩は 頭 がよくて、どんなこともわかりやすく説明してくれます。
／Our senior is smart; he can explain anything very clearly.
source_file: 中级上/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第31课.md

title: 〜おかげだ。<cause of a positive result>・〜せいだ。<cause of a negative result>
body_lines: Pattern: V attributive form ＋おかげだ（・せいだ）.
A / A attributive form ＋おかげだ（・せいだ）.
Ⅰ Ⅱ
N＋の＋おかげだ（・せいだ）。
The attributive form of a verb/adjective, or "noun+の", followed by "おかげだ" expresses the cause of
a positive result. It often appears as "〜おかげで、〜", with the latter clause describing how the speaker
concretely benefited. Translate as "thanks to...".
① 全部佐藤さんが教えてくれたおかげです。／It's all thanks to you, Sato, for teaching me.
② みんなが 協 力 してくれたおかげで、発表 がうまくいった。／thanks to; owing to
Thanks to everyone's help, the presentation went smoothly.
In contrast to "〜おかげだ", the attributive form or "noun+の" followed by "せいだ" expresses the cause of
a negative result. It can also appear as "〜せいで、〜" or "〜せいじゃない", meaning "it's all ...'s fault",
"just because of...", or "it's not ...'s fault".
③ 今回の失敗は、すべてわたしのせいです。／This failure is entirely my fault.
④ 君が遅れたせいで、プロジェクトは3 月までに完成できなかった。／
Because of your delays, the project wasn't finished before March.
source_file: 中级上/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第31课.md

title: V（よ）う <volitional form of verbs>
body_lines: The volitional form of a verb expresses the speaker's will, a suggestion, etc. Its conjugation rules are as follows:
Group I (godan) verbs:
Change the final u-dan kana of the verb to the corresponding o-dan kana and add "う". For example:
返す：かえす→そ＋う＝返そう
書く：かく→こ＋う＝書こう
急ぐ：いそぐ→ご＋う＝急ごう
待つ：まつ→と＋う＝待とう
読む：よむ→も＋う＝読もう
遊ぶ：あそぶ→ぼ＋う＝遊ぼう
送る：おくる→ろ＋う＝送ろう
Group II (ichidan) verbs:
Drop the final kana "る" of the verb and add "よう". For example:
辞める：やめる＋よう＝辞めよう
寝る：ねる＋よう＝寝よう
Group III (irregular) verbs:
(1) Suru-verbs: change "する" to "し" and add "よう". That is:
する：する→し＋よう＝しよう
勉強する：勉 強する→し＋よう＝勉強しよう
(2) Kuru-verb: change "来る" to "来" and add "よう". That is:
来る：くる→こ＋よう＝来よう
"V（よ）う" is the plain form of "Vましょう". It can express the speaker's own intention to do
the action, as in example ①; or that the speaker and listener do the action together, usually translated
as "let's ...", as in example ②. In Japanese, this pattern of doing something together is also often
used to suggest that the listener do something — a rather indirect, soft way of suggesting, as in example ③.
① Polite: 私も（本を）借りてきましょう。／I'll go borrow one too.
Plain: 私も（本を）借りてこよう。
② Polite: いっしょに映画を見に行きましょう。／Let's go see a movie together.
Plain: いっしょに映画を見に行こう。
③ Polite: 道を渡る時、横断歩道を使いましょう。／When crossing the road, use the crosswalk.
Plain: 道を渡る時、横断歩道を使おう。
source_file: 中级上/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第32课.md

title: V（よ）うと思う
body_lines: The volitional form followed by "と思う" gives "V（よ）うと思う", mostly used in the first person
to express the speaker's intention to do something — "I'm determined to..." / "I think I'll...". Unlike (what we learned in Lesson 19)
Compared with "V るつもりだ" (intend to do...) learned earlier, "V（よ）うと思う" uses the
volitional form "V（よ）う", so it more strongly reflects the speaker's
will and inner drive toward taking that action.
① 日本のアニメが大好きで、日本語を学ぼうと思いました。／I love
Japanese anime so much that I decided to learn Japanese.
② 運動しようと思って、ランニングシューズを買ってきました。／I wanted to get some exercise, so I bought a pair of running shoes.
I wanted to exercise, so I bought running shoes.
③ 今夜は久しぶりに映画を見ようと思います。／Tonight I think I'll watch a movie
for the first time in a while.
source_file: 中级上/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第32课.md

title: 〜たら、〜た。 <discovery>
body_lines: Pattern: V た + ら
Aい→かった+ら
Ⅰ
A +だったら
Ⅱ
N+だったら
We learned earlier that verbs, nouns, and adjectives followed by "たら" form a conditional. When the main
clause ends in the past tense — the "〜たら、〜た" pattern — it expresses that when the event before "たら"
occurred, the result in the latter clause turned out differently from what was expected. The latter clause is often
something beyond the speaker's control, a new discovery, or a surprise.
① 昼は暑かったのに、夜になったら、とても寒かった。／It was hot at noon,
but when evening came, it turned (surprisingly) cold.
② 買い物に行ったら、店は閉まっていた。／I went shopping, only to find the store
was closed.
③ 家に帰ったら、誰もいなかった。／When I got home, (I found) nobody was there.
source_file: 中级上/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第32课.md

title: 〜のに。 <dissatisfaction>
body_lines: We learned the adversative "のに" used mid-sentence. "のに" can also come at the end of a sentence,
expressing regret or dissatisfaction that the actual result differs from what was expected from the preceding clause.
It generally need not be translated.
① 必ず来ると約束してくれたのに。／He promised me he would definitely come. (and yet...)
② あと一分早ければ、終電に間に合ったのに。／If I'd been just one minute earlier,
I would have made the last train.
③ え？売り切れた？買いたかったのに。／Huh? Sold out? I really wanted to buy it.
source_file: 中级上/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第32课.md

title: って ＜quotation＞
body_lines: The particle "って" is the colloquial form of the quotation particle "と". Sometimes it can be used alone
with the following verb omitted, as in example ②.
① 今日は学校に行きたくないって言っていますよ。／(He) says he doesn't
want to go to school today.
② 母:お父さん何だって？／What did your dad say?
娘:フライトはキャンセルになったから、今夜は帰れないかもしれな
いって。／He said the flight was canceled, so he probably can't come back tonight.
③ メールしてねって言ったのに。／He told me to email him. (and yet...)
source_file: 中级上/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第32课.md

title: V てしまう
body_lines: A verb followed by "V てしまう" expresses the speaker's regret, remorse, or dismay that the action happened.
In colloquial speech, "V てしまう" also becomes "V ちゃう".
① クレジットカードをなくしてしまって、困っています。／I lost my credit card, and now I'm in trouble.
② いつもかぎを忘れてしまう。／I always end up forgetting my keys.
③ 言ってはいけないことを言っちゃった。どうしよう。／I said something I shouldn't have.
What should I do...
source_file: 中级上/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第32课.md

title: 〜ため（に）＜cause; reason＞
body_lines: Pattern: N＋の＋ため（に）、〜
A/A /V attributive form + ため（に）、〜
Ⅰ Ⅱ
"Noun + の" or the attributive form of a verb/adjective followed by "ため（に）" describes a cause.
When "ため（に）" describes a cause, the result is often unfavorable, and the tone is formal, mostly written.
① 台風が近づいているため、今日の学校は休みになりました。／Because a typhoon
is approaching, school is closed today.
② 事故のため、電車が遅れています。／The train is delayed due to an accident.
③ 今日の会議は出席者が少なかったため、早く終わった。／Today's meeting
ended early because attendance was low.
source_file: 中级上/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第32课.md

title: V ずに
body_lines: Pattern: V ない＋ずに
To attach "ずに" to a verb, use the continuative of the negative form: drop the "ない" of the nai-form;
for the Group III verb "する", it becomes "せず" before "ず".
"V ずに" is the written form of "Vないで" and modifies the following clause adverbially:
doing the latter action without (doing) the former.
① 一日も休まずに、一生懸命働いている。／(He) works incredibly hard without taking a single day off.
② この仕事は誰にも手伝ってもらわずに、自分で完成させた。／I completed this work
on my own, without help from anyone.
③ この夏休みはどこにも行かずに、家で仕事しようと思う。／This summer vacation
I plan to go nowhere and work at home.
source_file: 中级上/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第32课.md

title: 〜を V <passing through>
body_lines: Before an intransitive verb of movement, the particle "を" can mark the place passed through or moved across. For
example:
① アメリカを経由してブラジルへ行く。／Go to Brazil via the United States.
② 新宿で電車を降りよう。／Get off the train at Shinjuku.
③ 横断歩道を渡って、次の交差点を右に曲がると、銀行は右手にありま
す。／Cross the crosswalk, turn right at the next intersection, and the bank is on your right.
source_file: 中级上/13.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第32课.md

title: V（よ）うとする
body_lines: The volitional form of a volitional verb followed by "とする" can express that the first or third person,
as the agent, shows signs of being about to perform an action.
① 一日で平仮名とカタカナを全て覚えようとしましたが、できませんで
した。／I tried to memorize all the hiragana and katakana in one day, but couldn't do it.
② 宮崎駿監督はこのシーンで、宮沢賢治の作品『銀河鉄道の夜』のワン
シーンを描こうとしたそうです。／Director Miyazaki is said to have tried to depict in this scene
a scene from Miyazawa Kenji's "Night on the Galactic Railroad".
③ 多くの人があの企業 に入ろうとしています。／Many people are trying to get into that company.
The volitional form can also take the negative "としない", expressing that the third person shows no sign
of being willing to perform the action.
④ 先生は私の話を信じようとしない。／The teacher refuses to believe what I say.
⑤ うちの子は何度言っても勉強しようとしない。／No matter how many times I tell him,
my child shows no intention of studying.
In addition, the form "V（よ）うとした時" can be used to express the moment just before carrying out
the action — "just as I was about to...".
⑥ タクシーを降りようとした時、電話がかかってきた。／Just as I was about to get out of the taxi,
the phone rang.
source_file: 中级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第33课.md

title: Written-style continuation form of verbs
body_lines: We learned to use the te-form of verbs for sequential continuation, as in sentence a. This form is mostly
colloquial; in written Japanese or formal settings, the masu-stem of the verb can also express sequential
continuation, as in sentence b.
a. 留学していた時、昼は大学に通って、夜は働いていました。／While studying abroad,
I attended university during the day and worked at night.
b. 留学していた時、昼は大学に通い、夜は働いていました。
Note that the masu-stem used as a written continuative is limited to sequential sentences and cannot
combine with the negative form (V ない); when the masu-stem is a single syllable (e.g. "来", "見", "出"),
only the te-form can be used for continuation (as in example ③); the existential verb "いる" must first
be replaced by "おる" before its masu-stem can serve as a written continuative (as in example ④).
① 血液検査を行い、点滴をしていきましょう。／Let's do a blood test and put you on a drip.
② 銀行に行き、お金を下ろし、家賃を払いに行きました。／I went to the bank, withdrew money,
and went to pay the rent.
③ （○）後輩の結婚式に出て、スピーチをした。／I attended my junior's wedding
and gave a speech.
（×）後輩の結婚式に出、スピーチをした。
④ （○）フロントに係員がいて、事情説明をしています。／A staff member is at the front desk
explaining the situation.
（○）フロントに係 員がおり、事情説明をしています。
（×）フロントに係 員がい、事情説明をしています
source_file: 中级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第33课.md

title: N みたいだ ＜example; metaphor＞
body_lines: "みたいだ" attaches to a noun and, like "ようだ" learned in Lesson 25, is used for similes.
"〜みたいだ" is often paired with the adverb "まるで" — "just like...; as if..."
① 彼はどうしてあんなにわがままなことを言えるんですか。子供みたい
です。／How could he say something so selfish? He's just like a child.
② この格好、いいですね。映画のスターみたいですよ。／That outfit looks great —
like a movie star.
A noun followed by "みたい（だ）" can also cite another thing (often the subject) as an example that shares
the features of the thing before "みたい". For exemplification, the attributive form "〜みたいな" or the
adverbial form "〜みたいに" is usually used. For example:
③ あの学生みたいな人は誰ですか。／Who is that student-looking person?
④ もう秋なのに、真夏みたいに暑い。／It's already autumn, yet it's hot like midsummer.
source_file: 中级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第33课.md

title: N のような・N のように ＜example＞
body_lines: Besides the simile use from Lesson 25, "〜ようだ" can also give examples. Like "〜みたいだ",
when used for examples it modifies a following noun as "N のような", or a following verb/adjective
as "Nのように".
① 李さんのように日本語がペラペラに話せる人はなかなかいない。／Few people can speak Japanese as fluently as Li.
② 清華大学のようなキャンパスで大学時代を過ごしてみたい。／I'd love to spend my university years
on a campus like Tsinghua's.
③ 駅や空港のように人が多いところでは、自分の荷物の管理に気をつけ
ましょう。／In crowded places like stations and airports, keep an eye on your luggage.
In general, "みたいだ" after a noun for similes or examples is used similarly to "ようだ".
"みたいだ" is more colloquial.
source_file: 中级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第33课.md

title: 〜かぎり、〜＜limitation＞
body_lines: The attributive form followed by "かぎり" expresses that as long as the state before "かぎり" continues,
the state after it continues too.
① 体が丈夫なかぎり、社会活動を続けたい。／As long as my health holds up, I want to
keep doing volunteer work.
② A：そろそろ会議を始めようか。／Shall we start the meeting soon?
B：会議室では今、別の会議をやっているから、それが終わらないか
ぎり、使えないんだよ。／Another meeting is going on in the meeting room now, so as long as
it doesn't end, we can't use the room.
③ 彼がそばにいてくれるかぎり、わたしは安心していられる。／As long as he is by my side, I can feel at ease.
source_file: 中级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第33课.md

title: 〜というと、〜
body_lines: "というと" can follow a noun or plain sentence to present a topic, indicating what immediately comes
to mind when the preceding item is mentioned — "speaking of...; when you mention...". It can also be
used in conversation to pick up the other person's topic and offer your own thought.
① 日本料理というと、まず 頭に浮かぶのはお寿司や刺身ですよね。／
Speaking of Japanese food, sushi and sashimi are what first come to mind, right?
② A: 今年の忘年会は駅前の「焼き鳥屋」でやりましょうか。／Shall we hold this year's year-end party
at the "Yakitori-ya" in front of the station?
B: 「焼き鳥屋」というと、すごい人気で予約がなかなか取れない店で
すよね？／"Yakitori-ya" — you mean that super popular place that's hard to book, right?
③ 今年の夏の一番の思い出というと、初めて海外旅行に行ったことかも
しれません。／Speaking of this summer's most unforgettable memory, it would probably be my first trip
abroad.
source_file: 中级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第33课.md

title: 〜だろう
body_lines: Pattern: N/A/A /V plain form + だろう
Ⅰ Ⅱ
※N だ＋だろう
※A だ＋だろう
Ⅱ
"だろう" is the plain form of "でしょう", expressing conjecture — "probably...; ...I suppose; ...right?"
① 田中さんは今日のミーティングに来ないだろう。 忙 しいと言ってい
たから。／Tanaka probably won't come to today's meeting. He said he's busy.
② A：これはどうだろう。／How about this one?
B：Cさんが好きそうな色だから、きっと喜んでくれるだろうと思う
よ。／It's a color C would like — I'm sure he'll be happy.
③ この説明は 難 しいから、子供にはわからないだろう。／This explanation is too hard;
children probably won't understand it.
source_file: 中级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第33课.md

title: N をもとに（して）
body_lines: A noun followed by "をもとに（して）" expresses using the preceding content as a basis or source material
for a speech act or creative work — "based on...; drawing on...".
① 自分の体験をもとにしてスピーチの原稿を書いた方がいいと思う。／
I think I should write my speech based on my own experiences.
② 分析データをもとに、 新 しいシステムを導入 することにしました。
／Based on the analysis data, we introduced a new system.
③ このドレスは、富士山の 形 をもとにしてデザインしたものです。／
This dress was designed with reference to the shape of Mt. Fuji.
source_file: 中级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第33课.md

title: N をしている
body_lines: When describing that a person, animal, or object has a certain outward appearance, the form
"N をしている" can be used. Here the noun (N) is usually accompanied by a modifier describing
a concrete feature, for example:
① ちびまる子ちゃんは丸い顔をしています。／Chibi Maruko-chan has a round face.
② あの変な形をしている建物は何？／What's that oddly shaped building?
③ その猫は不思議な模様をしている。／That cat has mysterious markings.
④ 彼女はとても複雑な 表情 をしていて、何を 考 えているのかわから
ない。／She has a complicated look on her face; I can't tell what she's thinking.
source_file: 中级下/1.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第33课.md

title: The passive form of verbs
body_lines: The passive form of Japanese verbs is formed by attaching “れる” or “られる” to the verb stem. The specific conjuga-
tion rules are as follows:
Group I (godan) verbs:
Change the final u-row kana of the verb to the corresponding a-row kana and attach “れる”.
Note: verbs ending in “う” first change to “わ” before attaching “れる”. For example:
返す：かえす→さ＋れる＝返される
書く：かく→か＋れる＝書かれる
打つ：うつ→た＋れる＝打たれる
読む：よむ→ま＋れる＝読まれる
呼ぶ：よぶ→ば＋れる＝呼ばれる
送る：おくる→ら＋れる＝送られる
使う：つかう→わ＋れる＝使われる
Group II (ichidan) verbs:
Remove the final kana “る” of the verb and attach “られる”. For example:
集める：あつめる＋られる＝集められる
見る：みる＋られる＝見られる
Group III (irregular) verbs:
(1) Suru-verbs: change “する” to “される”. That is:
する：する→される
教育する：教 育する→教育される
(2) Kuru-verb: change “来る” to “来”, then attach “られる”. That is:
来る：来る→来＋られる＝来られる
source_file: 中级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第34课.md

title: Japanese passive sentences I: direct passive sentences <basic passive sentences A, B>
body_lines: In Japanese, a sentence whose subject is the agent of the action is called an “active sentence”, and one whose subject is the receiver of the
action is called a “passive sentence” (Japanese: 受け身文). The correspondence between Japanese “active sentences” and “passive sentences”
is as follows:
a. 先生が学生をほめました。<active>／The teacher praised the student.
b. 学生が先生にほめられました。<passive>／The student was praised by the teacher.
a. 上司は私に仕事を頼みました。<active>／The boss assigned me work.
（2） わたし じょうし しごと たの
b. 私は上司に仕事を頼まれました。<passive>／I was assigned work
by the boss.
In example (1-a), “先生” is the agent of the action “ほめる (to praise)”, while the
receiver of the action is “学生”, marked with the particle “を” in the active sentence. When converted to the passive sentence (1-b), the
receiver “学生” becomes the subject, marked with “は” or “が”; the agent
“先生” must be marked with the particle “に”, and the verb “ほめる” changes to its passive form “ほ
められる”. This pattern can be summarized as:
Direct passive sentence A: N が/は N に/から V（ら）れる
Here, N is the receiver of the action, marked with “が/は”; N is the agent, marked with “に/
から”. In basic passive sentences, both the receiver N and the agent N should be people.
In example (2-a), “上司” is the agent of the action “頼む”, while the receiver is
“私”, but the direct object of the predicate verb “頼む” is “仕事”. Therefore, in the passive sentence (2-b),
the direct object “仕事” of the predicate verb still needs to be marked with “を”; the receiver “私”
becomes the subject of the passive sentence, marked with “は” or “が”; the agent “上司” can
be marked with the particle “に” or “から”; the verb “頼む” changes to its passive form “頼まれる”.
This pattern can be summarized as:
Direct passive sentence B: N が/は N に/から N を V（ら）れる
Here, N is the receiver of the action, marked with “が/は”; N is the agent, marked with “に/か
ら”; N is the direct object of the action, marked with “を”. As with direct passive A, in direct pas-
sive B, both the receiver N and the agent N should be people.
Among the many types of Japanese passive sentences, the “direct passive” is semantically neutral, and its “active”
and “passive” versions can mostly be interchanged. For example:
① お母さんは子供を起こしました。／The mother woke the child up.
→子供はお母さんに起こされました。／The child was woken up by the mother.
② 日本政府は、高橋さんを招待した。／The Japanese government invited Takahashi.
→高橋さんは日本政府に 招待されました。／Takahashi was invited by the Japanese government.
③ （私は）友達に就 職のことについていろいろ聞かれました。／(I) was asked all sorts of things by a friend about job hunting.
④ （私は）人から嫌われるのが怖かった。／I was afraid of being disliked by people.
⑤ （私は）親から反対されても、彼女と結婚します。／Even if my parents object,
I will still marry her.
However, it is worth noting that when the agent of the verb is the first person, the active sentence is usually used rather than the passive.
For example:
⑥ （○）私は 妹 を呼びました。／I called my younger sister.
（×） 妹 は私に呼ばれました。
source_file: 中级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第34课.md

title: Japanese passive sentences II: possessor passive sentences
body_lines: The possessor passive is mainly used to describe that something belonging to the receiver of the action, or a part of their body, is affected by some ac-
tion. Possessor passive sentences often carry a clear sense of being adversely affected. The basic pattern is:
Possessor passive: N が/は N に N を V（ら）れる
Here, N is the possessor and also the receiver of the action; it serves as the subject of the possessor passive, marked with “が/は”;
N is N's possession or a part of the body — the direct object of the predicate verb, marked with “を”;
the agent N is marked with “に”.
① （私は）電車の中で足を踏まれました。／I had my foot stepped on in the train.
② （私は）パリの地下鉄で（すりに）財布を盗まれました。／In the Paris
metro, I had my wallet stolen (by a pickpocket).
③ 取っておいたケーキを 妹 に食べられてしまった。／The cake I had saved was eaten by my younger sister.
The Japanese possessor passive differs slightly from the Chinese passive in expression, so special attention is needed here.
In Japanese, the possessor and the possession (or body part) serve as the subject (which can be omitted) and the object of the
verb respectively; it cannot be expressed in the manner of example (4-b).
④ a.（○）（ 私 は） 弟 にパソコンを壊されました。／My computer was
broken by my younger brother.
b.（×）私のパソコンを 弟 に壊されました。
source_file: 中级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第34课.md

title: Japanese passive sentences III: indirect passive sentences
body_lines: The “indirect passive” refers to cases where the action does not directly affect the subject (mostly first person), but
the subject suffers or is troubled by some event or someone else's action — an indirect effect; some books also call it the “adversative
passive”. Since predicate verbs can be divided into intransitive and transitive verbs, the “indirect passive” has the following
two patterns:
Indirect passive (intransitive verb): N が/は N に V（ら）れる
Indirect passive (transitive verb): N が/は N に N を V（ら）れる
Here, N is the adversely affected party, serving as subject marked with “が/は”; N is the actor, marked with the particle “に”.
The indirect passive expresses that N suffers an adverse ef-
fect or damage due to some unintentional action of N. When N's action is a transitive verb, its object N is marked with “を”.
① 昨日の夜、隣の子供に泣かれて、よく眠れませんでした。／Last night, the neighbor's child kept crying, so I didn't sleep well.
② 遠足の日に雨に降られて、びしょびしょでした。／On the day of the excursion I got caught in the rain and
was soaked to the skin.
③ 夜遅くまで起きていることはできません。11時半に電気を消されてし
まいますから。／I can't stay up late at night, because the lights go out at 11:30.
④ やっとタクシーが来たのに、向こうにいた人に先に止められてしまっ
た。／A taxi finally came, but someone over there flagged it down first.
source_file: 中级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第34课.md

title: Japanese passive sentences IV: non-emotive passive sentences
body_lines: The Japanese “non-emotive passive” is closest in usage to the English passive. This is mainly due to the influence of the mass
translation and introduction of European and American literary works starting in the Meiji period, which gradually
popularized the use of the “non-emotive passive”.
The “non-emotive passive” is often used to state well-known social phenomena, with a thing or matter as the subject.
Depending on whether the agent of the action needs to be explicitly stated, the “non-emotive passive” can be divided into two types:
Non-emotive passive A (unspecified agent): N が/は（N に）V（ら）れる
Whether or not the agent (the doer of the action) is a specific person, the key fea-
ture of the “non-emotive passive” is that the subject N must be a “thing or matter”, marked with “が” or “は”. The agent is marked with “に”,
and since the agent is not a specific person, “N に” is generally omitted.
① この教会は600年前に建てられました。／This church was built 600 years ago.
② 日本語は多くの人に学ばれています。／Japanese is studied by many people.
③ 地震で、多くの家屋が壊されました。／Many houses were destroyed in the earthquake.
Non-emotive passive B (specified agent): N が/は N によって V（ら）れる
The “non-emotive passive B” is mainly used to describe inventions, creations, or new discoveries. In this case the
agent (doer of the action) N must be explicitly stated and marked with “によって”.
④ タバコはポルトガル人によって、日本に伝えられました。／Tobacco was introduced
to Japan by the Portuguese.
⑤ これは夏目漱石によって書かれた名小説です。／This is a famous novel written
by Natsume Soseki.
⑥ 『スズメの戸締り』は新海誠監督によって作られました。／Suzume was cre-
ated by director Shinkai Makoto.
source_file: 中级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第34课.md

title: 〜かどうか
body_lines: A plain-form sentence, or the stem of a na-adjective or a noun followed by “かどうか”, is used to present the two possibilities,
affirmative or negative. Equivalent to “whether or not ...”.
① 新しいスマホを買うかどうか、悩んでいます。／I'm agonizing over whether or not to
buy a new smartphone.
② 今、会議室が使われているかどうか聞いてきて。／Go ask whether the meeting room is
being used (by someone) right now.
③ 明日の部活を休んでもいいかどうか、誰に聞けばいいんですか。／Whether I can take tomorrow's club activity off — who should I ask?
source_file: 中级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第34课.md

title: たとえ〜ても
body_lines: “たとえ” is used together with the te-form of a verb followed by “ても” (or a noun followed by “でも”) to ex-
press that even if an extreme situation occurs, the conclusion in the second clause will not change. Can be translated as “even if ..., ...” or
“no matter ..., ...”.
① たとえ親に納得してもらえなくても、やりたいことはやる。／Even if my parents don't approve, I will do what I want to do.
② たとえコーヒーを５杯飲んでも、眠気が取れない。／Even if I drink 5 cups of coffee,
I can't shake off the drowsiness.
③ たとえ朝から晩まで 働 いても家は買えません。／Even if I work from morning
till night, I can't afford a house.
source_file: 中级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第34课.md

title: 〜ばかりでなく
body_lines: Pattern: N/A/A/V plain form + ばかりでなく
Ⅰ Ⅱ
※N だ＋ばかりでなく
※A だ＋な＋ばかりでなく
Ⅱ
A noun, or the attributive form of an adjective or verb, followed by “ばかりでなく” indicates that not only the first clause,
but the second clause also has the same situation or similar characteristics. Can be translated as “not only ..., but also ...”. In the second clause it is often paired with
“も” or “まで”.
① その行動は母の教えに反するばかりでなく、自分の気持ちにも反する
行動であった。／That action went against not only my mother's teachings, but also my own inner
feelings.
② これは私自身ばかりでなく、中国人はみんなそう思っていることだ。
／Not only I (think so) — all Chinese people think so.
③ 市民の努力で、繁華街のゴミが減ったばかりでなく、公園や道路もき
れいになった。／Thanks to the citizens' efforts, not only did litter in the busy districts decrease, but the parks and
roads became cleaner too.
source_file: 中级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第34课.md

title: N らしい <typical characteristics>
body_lines: A noun followed by “らしい” forms a derived adjective expressing that something has the typical characteristics of what the noun denotes.
① どうも今の世の中は、子供らしい子供が少ないような気がする。／In to-
day's society, there seem to be fewer children who are truly childlike.
② 彼女は女性らしくて可愛いです。／She is feminine and cute.
③ 今日はとても春らしい天気ですね。／Today's weather is really spring-like, isn't it?
source_file: 中级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第34课.md

title: V るものではない ＜advice; warning＞
body_lines: The dictionary form of a verb followed by “ものではない” is used to give advice, meaning “one should not (do) ...”.
Here, the standard for judging “whether one should” is not a personal subjective opinion, but is mostly based on social morality or common sense.
① 自分の価値は他人が決めるものではない。／Your own worth should not be decided
by others.
② 子供の手の届くところに、危険なものを置くものではない。／You should not
put dangerous things within children's reach.
③ 男は人の前で泣くものじゃない。／A man should not cry in front of others.
source_file: 中级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第34课.md

title: V るには ＜purpose＞
body_lines: The dictionary form of a verb followed by “には” expresses a compound concept of purpose and condition. “V るには” is
basically synonymous with “V るために”, expressing purpose. The second clause after “V るには” often expresses a necessary
condition, the means or method required to achieve the purpose of the first clause, or the effort that must be made.
① 日本語が上達するには、繰り返して練習しなければなりません。／
To improve your Japanese, you must practice repeatedly.
② 成功するには何事でも、本当に情熱があることじゃないと難しいで
す。／To succeed, whatever it is, it must be something you are truly passionate about; otherwise it is very
difficult.
③ 日本の大学院に留学するには、どうしたらいいでしょうか。／What should I
do to study at a graduate school in Japan?
source_file: 中级下/3.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第34课.md

title: The causative form of verbs
body_lines: The causative form of Japanese verbs is formed by attaching “せる” or “させる” to the verb stem. The specific conjuga-
tion rules are as follows:
Group I (godan) verbs:
Change the final u-row kana of the verb to the corresponding a-row kana and attach “せる”.
Note: verbs ending in “う” first change to “わ” before attaching “せる”. For example:
返す：かえす→さ＋せる＝返させる
書く：かく→か＋せる＝書かせる
打つ：うつ→た＋せる＝打たせる
読む：よむ→ま＋せる＝読ませる
呼ぶ：よぶ→ば＋せる＝呼ばせる
送る：おくる→ら＋せる＝送らせる
使う：つかう→わ＋せる＝使わせる
Type II verbs: remove the final kana “る” of the verb and attach “させる”. For example:
集める：あつめる＋させる＝集めさせる
見る：みる＋させる＝見させる
Group III (irregular) verbs:
(1) Suru-verbs: change “する” to “させる”. That is:
する：する→させる
勉強する：勉強する→勉強させる
(2) Kuru-verb: change “来る” to “来”, then attach “させる”. That is:
来る：来る→来＋させる＝来させる
source_file: 中级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第35课.md

title: Japanese causative sentences I: transitive causative sentences
body_lines: Causative sentences express making someone do something, allowing someone to do something, etc.; they can be translated as “let/make ... (some-
one) do ... (something)”. According to the transitive/intransitive distinction, Japanese causative sentences fall into “transitive causative
sentences” and “intransitive causative sentences”. The basic pattern of a “transitive causative sentence” is:
Transitive causative sentence: N は/が N に N を V（さ）せる
N is the causer, serving as subject marked with “は” or “が”; N is the causee (the doer of the action),
marked with the particle “に”; N is the direct object of the action, marked with “を”. For example:
① a. 店員が本を並べます。／The shop assistant arranges the books.
b. 本屋の主人が店員に本を並べさせます。／The bookstore owner has the shop assistant arrange the
books.
Example ①a is an active sentence: the doer of the action, “店員”, is the subject, and “並べる” is the action of the subject.
In contrast, example ①b is its causative sentence: here “本屋の主人” becomes the subject who makes the assistant arrange the
books, while the doer “店員” becomes the causee in the “transitive causative sentence”,
marked with “に”; the direct object of the action “並べる” is “本”, marked with “を”. It is worth
noting that Japanese causative sentences are mostly used for a superior causing a subordinate to act. When a subordinate asks a superior to do something,
the causative form is generally not used.
② 母親は息子に食器を洗わせました。／The mother had her son wash the dishes.
③ 幼稚園で、先生は子供たちに絵を書かせたり、漢字を書かせたりしま
す。／In kindergarten, the teacher has the children draw pictures and write kanji.
④ お母さんは美紀に早く彼氏を作らせようとしている。／The mother is trying to get Mi-
ki to find a boyfriend soon.
source_file: 中级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第35课.md

title: Japanese causative sentences II: intransitive causative sentences
body_lines: Intransitive causative sentences express making someone do something, allowing someone to do something, or causing someone to feel a cer-
tain emotion, etc.; they can be translated as “let/make ... (someone) ... (do something)”. When the causative verb in a Japanese causative sentence is in-
transitive, the doer of the action can be marked with “を” or “に”. The basic pattern is:
Intransitive causative sentence: N は/が N に/を V（さ）せる
N is the causer, serving as subject marked with “は” or “が”; N is the causee, and also
the doer of the action, marked with “を” or “に”. It is worth noting here that, when the doer's will
is disregarded and coercion is expressed, “を” is usually used (as in example ①); when the doer's will
is considered and permission is implied, the doer can be marked with “に” (as in example ②).
① コーチはもう走れないという選手を無理やり走らせた。／The coach forced a player
who said he couldn't run anymore to run.
② 次は私に走らせてください。／Next, please let me run.
③ 彼はまじめな顔でおもしろいことを言って、みんなを笑わせます。／
He says funny things in all seriousness, making everyone laugh.
④ 娘：お母さん、私も一人で外国に行ってもいい？／Daughter: Mom, can I
go abroad on my own too?
母：そうねえ、あなたにも行かせてあげたいけど、女の子だから、ち
ょっと心配。／Mother: Hmm..., I'd like to let you go, but since you're a girl,
I'm a little worried.
⑤ 心臓が弱いから、（ 私 を）びっくりさせないでくださいよ。／My heart is weak, so please don't scare me.
⑥ 小学生の時、隣 の子をいじめて泣かせたことを今も覚えている。／
I still remember how, in elementary school, I bullied the kid next to me and made him cry.
source_file: 中级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第35课.md

title: わけがない
body_lines: Pattern: A/A/V attributive form + わけがない
Ⅰ Ⅱ
N＋な＋わけがない
The attributive form of a declinable word, or “noun + な”, followed by “わけがない”, indicates that there is no reason for the
situation described before “わけ” to hold or exist; it can be translated as “impossible ...”, “no reason to ...”. In spoken language,
the form “わけない” can be used, as in the text, omitting the particle “が”.
① こんなに厚い本を一晩で読み終わるわけがないでしょ？／How could anyone possibly finish
reading such a thick book in one night?
② 普通のサラリーマンが高級 マンションを買えるわけがないよ。／An ordinary office worker can't possibly afford a luxury apartment.
③ 正直な王さんが嘘をつくわけがありません。／The honest Wang can't possibly
tell a lie.
source_file: 中级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第35课.md

title: N ばかり
body_lines: The particle “ばかり” follows a noun and emphasizes that there is nothing but the first item, ex-
pressing an extremely high quantity or degree of the first item, often with a negative feeling. Can be translated as “nothing but ...”, “only ...”.
① パソコンばかりいじらないでよ。／Don't keep fiddling with the computer all the time.
② お金のなかった時代は、ジャガいもばかり食べていた。／When I had no money,
I ate nothing but potatoes.
③ 梅雨に入ってから、毎日雨ばかりです。／Since the rainy season began, it has done nothing but
rain every day.
source_file: 中级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第35课.md

title: V てはじめて
body_lines: The te-form of a verb followed by “てはじめて” describes that only after the experience or event of the first clause
does one gain a new realization or understanding of the content described in the second clause. The first clause is mostly a precondition, and the second is mostly some-
thing that has not happened, or a rule, truth, etc.
In addition, the second clause of the “てはじめて” pattern can also be in the past tense, used to describe that only after the experience of the first clause
or the event occurred did one realize or understand something previously unnoticed or ungrasped.
① 大きな仕事は入念な 準備があってはじめて成功するのだ。／A great under-
taking succeeds only with careful preparation.
② スポーツは自分でやってみてはじめてそのおもしろさがわかるので
す。／With sports, only by trying them yourself can you understand their enjoyment.
③ 入院してはじめて健康のありがたさがわかりました。／Only after being hospitalized did I under-
stand how precious health is.
④ 海外に行ってはじめて自分の国について何も知らないことに気づい
た。／Only after going abroad did I realize I knew nothing about my own country.
source_file: 中级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第35课.md

title: N次第だ
body_lines: “次第だ” follows a noun and indicates that the result of the second clause is determined by the situation or state denoted by the noun of the first
clause. Can be translated as “it all depends on ...”, “... decides it”.
① どうするか、あなた次第です。／What to do is up to you.
② 果物が甘くなるかどうかは夏の天気次第です。／Whether the fruit turns sweet depends
on the summer weather.
③ 言葉の使い方次第で、相手に嫌われることもあるし、相手を楽しませ
ることもある。／Depending on your choice of words, you can either displease the other person or make them happy.
④ いい点数が取れるかどうか、君の努力次第です。／Whether you get a good score
depends on your own effort.
source_file: 中级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第35课.md

title: 〜ということだ
body_lines: Using “ということだ” at the end of a sentence means the speaker summarizes or draws a conclusion from information or facts obtained from the context.
It can also be used to take up the other person's words, summarize them oneself, and confirm with the other party. The usage of
“一石二鳥ってことね” in this lesson is the latter. “〜ということ”
can be shortened in spoken language to “〜っていうこと” or “〜ってこと”.
① 田中さんはまだ来ていませんか。つまり、また遅刻したということで
すね。／Tanaka hasn't come yet? In other words, he's late again, right?
② スタッフ：本日のメニューはこちらの A セットと B セットだけにな
ります。／Today's menu offers only the A set and the B set.
客：つまり、他に選択肢はないってことね。／In other words, there are no other
options.
③ 職員：閲覧コーナーの本や雑誌は館内だけの閲覧になります。／The books
and magazines in the reading corner may only be read inside the building.
客：つまり、持ち出してはいけないということですね。／In other words,
they can't be taken out, right?
source_file: 中级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第35课.md

title: いくら〜ても
body_lines: Pattern: いくら V ても
いくらAい→くても
Ⅰ
いくらA /N でも
Ⅱ
“いくら〜ても” forms an adversative conditional sentence: no matter how great the degree, the
result holds unaffected. Can be translated as “no matter how much ..., ...”, “whatever ..., ...”. Similar in meaning
is “どんなに〜ても”.
① いくら好きなものでも、毎日食べると飽きてしまう。／No matter how much you like something,
if you eat it every day you get tired of it.
② いくら 断 られても絶対に参加させるからね。／No matter how many times I'm refused,
I will definitely make (her) participate.
③ 文法が難しくて、いくら読んでもよくわからない。／The grammar is too hard; no matter
how much I read, I don't understand it.
④ 彼女が作った 料 理だから、どんなにまずくても、おいしそうに食べ
ないとだめだよ。／Because it's food your girlfriend made, no matter how bad it tastes, you have to look like
you're enjoying it.
source_file: 中级下/5.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第35课.md

title: わけではない ＜partial negation＞
body_lines: The attributive form of a verb or adjective followed by “わけではない/わけじゃない” is used to deny the inevitable conclusion drawn from the situation described in the current or
preceding text, emphasizing that this is not the case. Can be translated as “it is not
that ...”, “not necessarily ...”.
① 料理ができないわけではない。料理をする暇がないだけだ。／It's not that I can't cook. I just don't have time to cook.
② 書斎にたくさんの本が並べてあるが、全部読んだわけではない。／Many books are lined up in the
study, but I haven't read them all.
③ その仕事をやりたいわけではないけど、指名されたから引き受けたの
だ。／It's not that I wanted to do that job; I took it on only because I was named.
source_file: 中级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第36课.md

title: 〜はずだ
body_lines: Pattern: V/A/A attributive form + はずだ
Ⅰ Ⅱ
※N だ＋の＋はずだ
The attributive form of a verb or adjective, or “noun + の”, followed by “はずだ”, expresses the speaker's inference, based on ob-
jective circumstances or reasons, that a result should or must be so. Can be translated as “should ...”, “supposed to ...”.
① さっき上田さんは、お客さんが来たと言っていたから、今はお客さ
んと会議室にいるはずだよ。／Ueda said earlier that a guest had come, so he should
be in the meeting room with the guest now.
② 二年前はまだ 小学六年生だったから、今は 中学二年生のはずです。
／Two years ago she was still a sixth grader, so she should be in her second year of junior high now.
③ みんな傘をさしているから、まだ降っているはずです。／Everyone has their umbrella up, so it should still be raining.
source_file: 中级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第36课.md

title: 〜まま
body_lines: Pattern: V た + まま
N の+まま
A/A attributive form + まま
Ⅰ Ⅱ
“Verb + た”, “noun + の”, or the attributive form of an adjective followed by “まま” describes keeping the state of the first clause
unchanged, or performing the action of the second clause while the state of the first clause remains unchanged.
① 電気をつけたまま出かけました。／I went out with the lights on.
② この辺りはあまり開発されず、まだ 昔 のままです。／This area has not been developed
much and remains as it was in the old days.
③ このきのこは生のままでは食べられません。／This mushroom cannot be eaten raw.
④ あの家はこの前の地震以来、壊れたままです。／That house has remained damaged since
the last earthquake (unrepaired).
source_file: 中级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第36课.md

title: 〜上で
body_lines: Pattern: V る + 上で
サ変V する＋の＋上で
The basic form of a verb, or a suru-verb stem, followed by “上で” expresses purpose. The first clause of
“〜上で” is mostly a positive purpose; the second clause describes the action that must be taken to achieve the purpose or goal of the first clause,
or an important consideration.
① 外国語学習 の上で 最 も大切なことは、その言語を使う環境 に身を
置くことです。／The most important thing in learning a foreign language is to place yourself in an environment
where that language is used.
② ダイエットをする上で 重要なことは、強い意志だと思います。／When it comes to dieting, I think what matters is having a strong will.
③ 面接を受ける上で 注意すべき点を教えてください。／Please tell me the points to keep in
mind when taking an interview.
source_file: 中级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第36课.md

title: N (+ particle) さえ
body_lines: “さえ” follows a noun or “noun + particle” and cites an extreme case to show that other cases
are all the more so. Can be translated as “even ...”.
① 好きなことさえわからないから、どうしよう。／I don't even know what I like —
what should I do?
② 足が痛くて、立っていることさえできない。／My feet hurt so much I can't even stand.
③ 私 にさえ話してくれないから、いくら聞いても言わないと思うよ。
／He won't even tell me, so I don't think he'll tell you no matter how you ask.
source_file: 中级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第36课.md

title: の <subject of a subordinate clause>
body_lines: The subject within an attributive modifier clause formed by a subject-predicate structure can be marked with the particle “の”. But if
using “の” would cause misunderstanding, “が” must still be used to mark the subject (as in example ②).
① これは去年佐藤さんの送ってくれた誕生日プレゼントです。／This is
the birthday present Sato sent me last year.
② 中村さんがお父さんに縫った財布はとてもおしゃれだった。／The wallet Nakamura sewed for
his father was very stylish.
③ 自分の 憧 れている人のしていることや自分のできそうなことをまず
書き出してみよう。／First, write down what the people you admire do, and what you can
do.
④ あなたのしたこと、誰も知らないと思ってるの？／Do you think nobody knows what you did?
that nobody else knows?
source_file: 中级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第36课.md

title: N に向かって
body_lines: A noun followed by “に向かって” indicates the direction of an object's movement, or the direction in which things develop and change. Can be
translated as “toward ...”.
① 飛行機は現在ワシントンに向かって速いスピードで進んでいます。／
The plane is currently heading for Washington at great speed.
② 両国の関係は良い方向に向かっている。／Relations between the two countries are heading in a good direc-
tion.
③ 目標を決めたら、その目標に向かって、ひたすら頑張る。／Once you've set a
goal, work single-mindedly toward it.
source_file: 中级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第36课.md

title: 〜の？
body_lines: In plain-form conversation, the sentence-final particle “の” expresses a question and can be used by both men and women. In this
case, use rising intonation.
① A：また夜更かしをしたの？／Did you stay up late again?
B：うん、ずっとゲームをしてたんだ。／Yeah, I was gaming the whole time.
② A：なにかあったの？／Did something happen?
B：別に。／Nothing really.
source_file: 中级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第36课.md

title: –出す
body_lines: The masu-stem of a verb followed by “出す” forms a compound verb, implying the beginning of an action or state, or bringing it to the sur-
face. Fairly close to “start ...-ing” or “... out” in English. For example:
① 理想と現実を全部書き出してみよう。／Let's write out all our ideals and
realities.
② あの子は警察官の顔を見ると、 急 に大声で泣き出した。／As soon as the child
saw the police officer's face, he suddenly burst out crying loudly.
③ 遊園地に連れて行ってあげると言ったら、「嬉しい！」と言って、踊り
出した。／When I said I'd take him to the amusement park, he cried “Yay!” and started dancing for joy.
source_file: 中级下/7.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第36课.md

title: The causative-passive form of verbs
body_lines: Besides the causative and passive forms we learned earlier, Japanese verbs also have a
“causative-passive form” formed by combining the causative and the passive. To make the causative-passive, first change the verb to its caus-
ative form, and then change that into the passive. The specific rules are as follows:
Type I verbs: Type I verbs have two ways of conjugating.
First: change the final u-row kana of the verb to the corresponding a-row kana and attach “せられる”. Note that verbs ending in
“う” first change to “わ” before attaching “せられる”. For example:
書く：かく→か＋せられる＝書かせられる
読む：よむ→ま＋せられる＝読ませられる
使う：つかう→わ＋せられる＝使わせられる
Second: change the final u-row kana of the verb to the corresponding a-row kana and attach “される”. This form is more col-
loquial.
書く：かく→か＋される＝書かされる
読む：よむ→ま＋される＝読まされる
使う：つかう→わ＋される＝使わされる
Note! Verbs ending in “す”, such as “話す”, “直す”, “出す”, “消す”, etc.,
are conjugated into the causative-passive using the first method above. For example:
話す：はなす→さ＋せられる＝話させられる
（×）話さされる
Group II (ichidan) verbs:
Remove the final kana “る” of the verb and attach “させられる”. For example:
集める：あつめる＋させられる＝集めさせられる
見る：みる＋させられる＝見させられる
Group III (irregular) verbs:
(1) Suru-verbs: change “する” to “させられる”. That is:
する：する→させられる
勉強する：勉強する→勉強させられる
(2) Kuru-verb: change “来る” to “来”, then attach “させられる”. That is:
来る：来る→来＋させられる＝来させられる
source_file: 中级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第37课.md

title: Causative-passive sentences
body_lines: Simply put, the causative-passive sentence is closer to an active sentence. For example:
① a. 私は漫画を捨てた。<active>
b. 私は漫画を捨てさせられた。<causative-passive>
In the examples above, the doer of the action in both a and b is “私”, and the action is the same: throwing away the manga.
Using the causative-passive form of the verb highlights the doer's psychological unwillingness and
displeasure when performing the action. The basic pattern of the causative-passive sentence is:
N は/が N に/から/によって N を V（さ）せられる
Here, N is the doer of the action, serving as subject marked with “は” or “が”; N is the
causer, i.e. the person or organization that makes N do something, usually marked with “に”; when emphasis on a
specific causer is needed, “から” or “によって” can also be used. But in causative-passive sentences, the causer
is generally omitted — example ①b omits it; N is the direct object of the action — in example ①b,
“漫画の本” is the direct object of the action “捨てる”, marked with “を”.
② 子供のころは、嫌いなものでも親に食べさせられました。／When I was a child,
my parents made me eat things even if I didn't like them.
③ この子には心配させられることが多い。冒険が好きな子なのだ。／This
child makes me worry a lot. He's a child who loves adventure.
④ この仕事は初めてなのに、一人で全部やらされました。／Although this job was
my first time, I was made to do it all by myself.
source_file: 中级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第37课.md

title: 〜ものだから
body_lines: The plain form of a verb or adjective followed by “ものだから” is used to state a reason. The pat-
tern “ものだから” is mostly used in spoken language, often to gently offer an excuse. Note that the second
clause after “ものだから” cannot express the speaker's will, commands, etc. When “ものだから” appears mid-sentence, the
form “もので” can also be used.
① A：顔色が悪いよ。／You look pale.
B：ええ、風邪を引いてしまったものですから、調子がよくないんで
す。／Yeah, I caught a cold, so I'm not in great shape.
② 彼は新人なもので、まだ社内のルールがよくわかっていない。／He's a
newcomer, so he doesn't know the company rules well yet.
③ 急 な 出 張 が入ってしまったものですから、今日の飲み会は欠席し
ます。／Since a sudden business trip came up, I can't make today's dinner party.
source_file: 中级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第37课.md

title: V てからでないと
body_lines: The te-form of a verb followed by “てからでないと” indicates that something is no good unless the first clause is completed first —
the first clause must be done first. The second clause is mostly negative in content. Can be translated as “unless ...
(first), (not) ...”. “てからでないと” can also be written as “てからでなけれ
ば”. Sometimes the second clause of “てからでないと” can be omitted.
① このアプリをインストールしてからでないと、携帯に入れた音楽は聞
けません。／You must install this app first, or you can't listen to the music stored on your phone.
② 鶏肉は 十分火が通ってからでないと、食べられません。／Chicken must be
cooked through before it can be eaten.
③ 全ての書類が揃ってからでないと、申し込みができません。／You must have all
the documents ready before you can apply.
source_file: 中级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第37课.md

title: って <topic>
body_lines: “って” is used to introduce a topic or present a theme, mostly in spoken language. Equivalent to “〜というの
は”, “〜は”, etc.
① N2の文法って難しいね。（って＝は）／N2 grammar is so hard, isn't it?
② 田中さんってどんな人なの？（って＝は）／What kind of person is Tanaka?
③ 毎日雨が降るってほんとに嫌だね。（って＝というのは）／Raining every day —
how annoying, right?
④ 人を案内するって、簡単なようで、案外疲れるよね。（って＝というの
は）／Showing people around seems simple, but it's surprisingly tiring.
source_file: 中级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第37课.md

title: 〜あげく
body_lines: Pattern: V た + あげく
N の+あげく
The ta-form of a verb, or an action “noun + の”, followed by “あげく”, indicates that after going through the process
described in the first clause, the result described in the second clause is finally reached. The first clause often implies repeated attempts,
a long time spent, or great effort, while the second clause is mostly a regrettable result. Can be translated as “...,
and in the end ...”, “after ..., ended up ...”.
“あげく” can also be used with the following predicate in the forms “あげくに” or “あげくの果てに”.
It can also modify a following noun in the form “あげくの”.
① 彼と口げんかを繰り返したあげく、別れることになった。／After repeated quarrels with my boyfriend, I ended up breaking up with him.
They often quarreled and finally broke up.
② かわいそうな 修二君。お金のことや友人の問題でさんざん親に心配
をかけたあげくに、とうとう家を出てしまった。／Poor Shuji. Causing his
parents endless worry over money and friends, he finally left home.
③ 戦争中 は、栄養失調 のあげく、亡くなってしまった人が多くいる。
／During the war, many people died of malnutrition.
④ 田中君は何度も遅刻や欠席を繰り返したあげくの果てに、退学処分に
なってしまった。／Tanaka repeated lateness and absences many times and was finally expelled.
⑤ 新発売のゲームを買いに来たが、開店前から 長時間並んで待たされ
たあげく、結局 売り切れになって買えなかった。／I came to buy the newly released game and was made to
queue for hours before opening, only to find it sold out — I couldn't buy it.
source_file: 中级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第37课.md

title: 〜うちに・〜ないうちに（Ⅰ）
body_lines: Pattern: N の + うちに
Aい+うちに
Ⅰ
A な+うちに
Ⅱ
V る/V ない+うちに
“Noun + の”, the attributive form of an adjective, or the dictionary form or ない-form of a verb followed by “うちに” in-
dicates performing the action of the second clause, or describing its state, within the period indicated by the first clause. Can be translated as “while
① 独身のうちに、スペインへ語学留学に行きたい。／While I'm still single, I want to go to
Spain to study the language.
② 今のうちに、いろいろ経験してみないとね。／You should try all sorts of experi-
ences while you can.
③ 「鉄は熱いうちに打て」という 諺 は、人は柔軟性のある若いうち
に、鍛えることが大事だという教えだ。／The proverb “strike while the iron is hot” teaches
that it is important to train yourself while you are young and flexible.
④ 忘れないうちに言っておくけど、例の件、延期になりました。／Before I
forget, let me mention: that matter has been postponed.
source_file: 中级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第37课.md

title: 〜うちに・〜ないうちに（Ⅱ）
body_lines: Pattern: N の + うちに
V る/V ない/V ている+うちに
In addition, “うちに” can follow “noun + の”, the dictionary form or ない-form of a verb, or
durative expressions such as the “verb ている” form, indicating that while the state of the first clause
continues, an unforeseen result or change described by the second clause occurs. Here “〜うち
に” is similar in meaning to “〜間に”.
① テレビを見ているうちに寝てしまいました。／I fell asleep while watching TV.
② 知らないうちに、バッグがなくなっていました。／Before I knew it, my bag was
gone.
③ ふと外を見ると、気がつかないうちに雨が降り出していた。／When I suddenly looked outside — before I knew it, it had started raining.
source_file: 中级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第37课.md

title: 上（に） ＜in addition＞
body_lines: Pattern: V/A/A attributive form + 上（に）
Ⅰ Ⅱ
N の/である+上（に）
The attributive form of a declinable word, or “noun + の/である”, followed by “上（に）”, indicates that, on top of the existing
state or event described in the first clause, something even better (or worse) also occurs. Can be translated as “...
and moreover ...”, “not only ..., but also ...”.
① 先輩には彼女を 紹介してもらった上に、結婚式の時に高価なお祝い
までいただいた。／My senior not only introduced me to my girlfriend, but also gave us a valuable
wedding gift at our wedding.
② この電話のプランにすると、電話がかけ放題の上、インターネットも
使い放題です。／With this phone plan, you get not only unlimited calls,
but also unlimited internet.
③ この映画は迫力 がある上に、泣けるシーンがたくさんあって、おす
すめだよ。／This movie is not only powerful but also has lots of tear-jerking scenes — highly recom-
mended.
④ 彼の話は長い上に、要点がはっきりしないから、みんな彼の話を聞
きたがらない。／His talks are long and lack a clear point, so nobody wants to listen to him.
source_file: 中级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第37课.md

title: 〜はもちろん
body_lines: A noun followed by “はもちろん”, or a noun plus particle followed by “はもちろん”, indicates that the representative thing of the first clause goes without
saying, and things in the second clause with similar qualities are likewise so. It usually appears as “〜はも
ちろん、…も…”, and can be translated as “... goes without saying, and ... (also) ...”.
① 日本語を上達させるには、復習はもちろん、予習もしなければいけ
ません。／To improve your Japanese, review goes without saying — you must also preview.
② 「ワンピース」は日本人にはもちろん、外国人にも人気がある漫画で
す。／“One Piece” is a manga popular not only among Japanese but also among
foreigners.
③ あの男は、盗みはもちろん、殺人もしたことがあるらしい。／That man
is said to have not only stolen but even killed someone.
④ うちの旦那は洗濯はもちろん、 料理もしてくれる。／My husband not only does the
laundry but also cooks for me.
source_file: 中级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第37课.md

title: V たらどうですか <invitation/suggestion>
body_lines: The ta-form of a verb followed by “たらどうですか” is used to suggest that the listener do something. When the two speakers are close,
“どうですか” is often omitted, using just “V たら?”, usually with rising
intonation at the end.
① 会社の仕事でも手伝ったら？／Why not help with the company work?
② そんなに嫌なら、やめたらどうですか。／If you hate it that much, why not
quit?
③ もう遅いから、残りは明日にしたらどう？／It's late already — how about leaving the rest for to-
morrow?
source_file: 中级下/9.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第37课.md

title: Imperative form of verbs
body_lines: Japanese verbs can express a forceful command through the imperative form. The conjugation rules are as follows:
Group I (godan) verbs:
Change the final u-dan kana of the verb to the corresponding e-dan kana. For example:
書く：かく→け＝書け
読む：よむ→め＝読め
使う：つかう→え＝使え
Group II (ichidan) verbs:
Drop the final kana "る" of the verb and add "ろ" (mostly spoken) or "よ" (mostly
written). For example:
食べる：たべる＋ろ＝食べろ
（或）たべる＋よ＝食べよ
見る：みる＋ろ＝見ろ
（或）みる＋よ＝見よ
Group III (irregular) verbs:
(1) Suru-verbs: change "する" to "しろ" (mostly spoken) or "せよ"
(mostly written). That is:
する：する→しろ
（或）→せよ
勉強する：勉強 する→勉強しろ
（或）→勉強せよ
(2) Kuru-verb: change "来る" to "来い". That is:
来る：来る→来い
Note that commands using the imperative form are mostly masculine speech, or used in specific situations:
giving orders (e.g. an officer to soldiers), cheering or warning at sporting events, and on warning
signs and notice boards.
① （サッカー場で）今がチャンスだ。行け！／(On the soccer field) Now's our chance.
Go!
② （交通標識）止まれ！／(Traffic sign) Stop!
③ （試験の問題用紙）次の文を英語に翻訳せよ。／(Exam paper) Translate the following
sentences into English.
source_file: 中级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第38课.md

title: V なさい
body_lines: The masu-stem of a verb followed by "なさい" gives a command or instruction, softer than the imperative.
It is generally used only from parents to children, teachers to students, superiors to subordinates, or between
close relations. "する" + "なさい" allows both "練習しなさい" and "練習なさい".
① 明日早いから、早く寝なさい。／You have to get up early tomorrow — go to bed early.
② 二人とも、喧嘩はやめなさい。／Both of you, stop fighting.
③ （試験の問題用紙）次の文を読んで、質問に回答しなさい。／（exam; test
(Exam question) Read the following passage and answer the questions.
source_file: 中级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第38课.md

title: Prohibitive form
body_lines: Opposite to the imperative, Japanese verbs also have a prohibitive form meaning "do not do..."
It is formed by adding "な" to the dictionary form. Likewise, prohibitive commands are mostly
masculine speech, or used in orders, sports cheering, warnings, and notice boards.
① 危険！近づくな。／Danger! Keep away.
② 秘密だから、絶対に人に言うなよ。／It's a secret — absolutely don't tell anyone.
③ 関係ないことを聞くな。／Don't ask about things that don't concern you.
source_file: 中级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第38课.md

title: 〜くらい ＜degree＞
body_lines: The plain form of a verb or adjective (mainly i-adjectives and dictionary forms) followed by "くらい"
cites a concrete case to illustrate the degree of the thing or state just described. "くらい" can
be replaced by "ほど".
① そんなの困るよ。泣きたいくらいだよ。／That's so troublesome. I could cry.
② 歩けないくらい膝が痛い。／My knees hurt so much I can't walk.
③ 目まいがするほどお腹が空いた。／I was so hungry I felt dizzy.
source_file: 中级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第38课.md

title: 〜通り（に）
body_lines: Pattern: V る/V た + 通り（に）
N の+通り（に）
N+通り（に）
The dictionary form, ta-form of a verb, or "noun + の" followed by "通り（に）" means doing something
exactly as the preceding instruction or example — "just as...; exactly like...". Note that when a noun
directly takes "通り（に）", it is read "どおり（に）". The form "〜通りのN" can also modify a noun.
① お医者さんの言う通りにしてください。／Please do as the doctor says.
② 「尽力」とは、文字通り「力を尽くす」という意味です。／“尽力” means, literally, “to exert one's strength to the fullest”.
③ 奥さんはわたしの想像した通りの 美 しい方でした。／His wife was just as beautiful
as I had imagined.
④ スピード違反で捕まってしまった。警察官に言われた通りに、後で
罰金を払った。／I got caught speeding. As the police officer told me, I later paid the fine.
source_file: 中级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第38课.md

title: 〜がちだ
body_lines: Pattern: V ます stem ＋がちだ
N＋がちだ
A noun or the masu-stem of a verb followed by "がちだ" expresses that something tends to happen easily,
or a tendency toward something. Generally used for negative situations.
① いつも車を使うから、運動不足になりがちです。／I always drive, so I tend to
lack exercise.
② 田中さんは物事を甘く 考 えがちだ。もっと現実をしっかりみたほう
がいいと思う。／Tanaka tends to take things too lightly. I think he should face
reality more squarely.
③ 謙遜しすぎて目立たずに過小 評価されがちの人もいれば、自慢話
をしすぎて過小 評 価されがちの人もいる。／Some people are easily underrated because they are
too modest and inconspicuous; others because they boast too much.
④ 親は子供のすることにいちいち口を出しがちです。黙って見守ってい
てあげることも大切だ。／Parents tend to meddle too much in their children's affairs. Quietly watching
over them matters too.
source_file: 中级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第38课.md

title: なぜなら（ば）〜からだ
body_lines: The pattern "なぜなら（ば）〜からだ" explains the preceding statement. Mostly written language —
"The reason is that...". In speech, "なぜかというと〜からだ" is more common.
① 今はなんとも言えない。なぜなら、まだ検討中だからだ。／I can't say anything yet.
Because it's still under discussion.
② わたしは 車 は要らない。なぜなら、うちには 駐車場 がないからで
す。／I don't need a car. Because we don't have a parking space at home.
③ 妻と離婚することになった。なぜなら、会社を首になったからだ。／
I ended up divorcing my wife. Because I was fired from the company.
④ 卵 を使わないで作ってください。なぜなら、 私 は 卵 アレルギーだ
からです。／Please don't make it with eggs. Because I'm allergic to eggs.
source_file: 中级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第38课.md

title: 〜がる
body_lines: Japanese adjectives of emotion can only be used for the first person. To state a third person's feelings
or mental state, add "がる" to the adjective stem to form an emotion verb. Note that when the subject
is first person, the object of the emotion adjective is marked with "が" (as in ①a); when the subject
becomes third person, the adjective turns into a "がる" verb, so the object is marked with "を" instead
(as in ①b).
① a. 私は犬が怖いです。／I'm afraid of dogs.
b. あの子は犬を怖がっています。／That child is scared of dogs.
② 近所には犬を嫌がる人がいます。／Some people in the neighborhood dislike dogs.
③ 張 さんは面接に失敗したことを残念がっていました。／Zhang was sorry that he had failed
the interview.
source_file: 中级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第38课.md

title: に <agent of ability>
body_lines: The particle "に" follows a person and precedes a verb of ability, marking the one who has (or lacks) the ability.
① まだ若いから、君にはわからないよ。／You're still young — you wouldn't understand.
② この本は 難 しくて、まだ初心者のわたしにはとても読めるようなも
のではない。／This book is too difficult — a beginner like me can't understand it at all.
③ 自分の家がほしいけれど、サラリーマンの 私 には到底買えるような
値段ではない。／I'd love a house of my own, but for an office worker like me,
the price is simply out of reach.
source_file: 中级下/11.梁爽老师日语精讲精练：第38课.md

title: 〜と思われる <spontaneous form of verbs>
